title.zh: 卷七十九 列傳第六十七: 宇文述 王世充 段達
title.en: Volume 79 Biographies 67: Yu Wenshu, Wang Shichong, Duan Da
title.raw: 卷七十九 列傳第六十七: 宇文述 王世充 段達 Volume 79 Biographies 67: Yu Wenshu, Wang Shichong, Duan Da

sentences.zh: 宇文述 王世充 段達

translations.literal: Yu Wenshu, Wang Shichong, Duan Da
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenshu, Wang Shichong, and Duan Da

sentences.zh: 列傳第六十七

translations.literal: Biography number sixty-seven
translations.idiomatic: Biography 67

sentences.zh: 宇文述雲定興趙行樞述子化及司馬德戡裴虔通王世充段達

translations.literal: Yu Wenshu, Yun Dingxing, Zhao Xingshu, Shu's son Huaji, Sima Dekan, Pei Qiantong, Wang Shichong, Duan Da
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenshu; Yun Dingxing; Zhao Xingshu; Yu Huaji, son of Wenshu; Sima Dekan; Pei Qiantong; Wang Shichong; and Duan Da

sentences.zh: 宇文述，字伯通，代郡武川人也。

translations.literal: Yu Wenshu, style name Botong, was a man of Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Wenshu, courtesy name Botong, was a native of Wuchuan in Dai Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖侰與敦、曾祖長壽、祖孤，仕魏，並為沃野鎮軍主。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi and Dun, great-great-grandfather Changshou, and grandfather Gu served Wei and were all garrison commanders at Woye Fortress.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yi and Dun, his great-great-grandfather Changshou, and his grandfather Gu all served Northern Wei as garrison commanders at Woye Fortress.

sentences.zh: 父盛，仕周，位上柱國、大宗伯。

translations.literal: His father Sheng served Zhou, holding the posts of Supreme Pillar of State and Grand Director of Honors.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng served Northern Zhou, rising to Supreme Pillar of State and Grand Director of Honors.

sentences.zh: 述少驍銳，便弓馬。

translations.literal: Shu in youth was fierce and sharp, skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Wenshu was bold and keen, expert with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 年十一時，有相者謂曰：「公子善自愛，後當位極人臣。」

translations.literal: At age eleven a physiognomist said to him: "Young lord, take good care of yourself; later you will reach the utmost rank among ministers."
translations.idiomatic: When he was eleven, a physiognomist told him, "Young lord, cherish yourself—you will one day stand at the pinnacle of power among ministers."

sentences.zh: 周武帝時，以父軍功，起家拜開府。

translations.literal: In Emperor Wu of Zhou's time, through his father's military merit, he began his career and was appointed Opening the Government.
translations.idiomatic: During the reign of Emperor Wu of Northern Zhou, he entered service on his father's military record and was appointed an honorary commander of an independent staff.

sentences.zh: 述性謹密，周大塚宰宇文護甚愛之，以本官領護親信。

translations.literal: Shu's nature was careful and close; Zhou's Grand Chancellor Yuwen Hu greatly favored him and had him hold his original office while leading the Protector's trusted attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu was discreet by nature. Yuwen Hu, the Grand Chancellor of Northern Zhou, favored him greatly and let him keep his existing post while commanding the Protector's personal guard.

sentences.zh: 及武帝親總萬機，召為左宮伯，累遷英果中大夫，賜爵博陵郡公，改封濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu personally took charge of all affairs, he was summoned as Left Palace Bearer, promoted in succession to Valiant Fruit Central Grand Master, enfeoffed as Duke of Boling Commandery, and then re-enfeoffed as Duke of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took personal control of government, Wenshu was summoned as Left Palace Bearer, then promoted step by step to Valiant Fruit Central Grandee, enfeoffed as Duke of Boling, and later transferred to Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥作亂，述以行軍總管從韋孝寬擊之，破迥將李雋軍於懷州，又與諸將破尉惇于永平橋。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jiong raised rebellion; Shu as campaign commander-general followed Wei Xiaokuan to strike him, defeating Jiong's general Li Jun's army at Huai Prefecture, and again with the other generals defeating Wei Dun at Yongping Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled, Wenshu served as campaign commander under Wei Xiaokuan, routed Li Jun's forces at Huai Prefecture, and with the other generals defeated Wei Dun at Yongping Bridge.

sentences.zh: 以功超拜上柱國，進爵褒國公。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted beyond rank to Supreme Pillar of State and advanced in title to Duke of the State of Bao.
translations.idiomatic: For these deeds he was promoted in one leap to Supreme Pillar of State and advanced to Duke of Bao.

sentences.zh: 開皇初拜右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was appointed Right Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Kaihuang era he was made Right Guard Grand General.

sentences.zh: 平陳之役，以行軍總管自六合而濟。

translations.literal: In the campaign to pacify Chen, as campaign commander-general he crossed from Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: During the conquest of Chen he crossed the river from Liuhe as campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 時韓擒、賀若弼兩軍趣丹陽，述據石頭以為聲援。

translations.literal: At that time Han Qin and He Ruobi's two armies pressed toward Danyang; Shu held Shitou as a supporting shout.
translations.idiomatic: While Han Qin and He Ruobi drove on Danyang, Wenshu held Stone City to lend them support.

sentences.zh: 陳主既禽，而蕭瓛、蕭岩據東吳地。

translations.literal: After the Chen ruler was captured, Xiao Huan and Xiao Yan held the lands of eastern Wu.
translations.idiomatic: After the Chen emperor was taken, Xiao Huan and Xiao Yan still held eastern Wu.

sentences.zh: 述領行軍總管元契、張默言等討之，落叢公燕榮以舟師自東海至，亦受述節度，於是吳會悉平。

translations.literal: Shu led campaign commanders Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and others to attack them; Duke of Luocong Yan Rong came from the Eastern Sea with a fleet and also received Shu's command, and thus Wu and Kuai were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu led Yuan Qi, Zhang Moyan, and other commanders against them; Yan Rong, Duke of Luocong, arrived by sea from the Eastern Sea and likewise fell under his command, and Wu and Kuai were fully pacified.

sentences.zh: 以功授子化及為開府，徙拜安州總管。

translations.literal: For merit his son Huaji was granted Opening the Government, and he was transferred and appointed Anzhou Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: For his service his son Huaji was granted an independent staff, and Wenshu himself was transferred to commander-in-chief of Anzhou.

sentences.zh: 時晉王廣鎮揚州，甚善於述，奏為壽州總管。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Jin Guang was stationed at Yangzhou and was very friendly with Shu; he memorialized to make him Shouzhou Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jin Guang was then posted at Yangzhou and took a strong liking to Wenshu, recommending him as commander-in-chief of Shouzhou.

sentences.zh: 王時陰有奪宗之志，請計於述。

translations.literal: The prince at the time secretly harbored the will to seize the succession and asked Shu for plans.
translations.idiomatic: The prince already harbored secret designs on the succession and sought Wenshu's counsel.

sentences.zh: 述曰：「皇太子失愛已久。

translations.literal: Shu said: "The crown prince has long lost favor.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu said, "The crown prince has long since lost the emperor's favor.

sentences.zh: 大王才能蓋世，數經將領，主上之與內宮，咸所鍾愛，四海之望，實歸大王。

translations.literal: Your Highness's talent covers the age, you have repeatedly led armies, the sovereign and the inner palace alike cherish you, and the hopes of the four seas truly return to Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: Your talent outshines the age, you have led armies again and again, and both the emperor and the inner palace favor you—the empire's hopes truly rest on you.

sentences.zh: 然廢立國家大事，能移主上者，唯楊素耳。

translations.literal: Yet deposing and establishing is a great affair of state; the one who can move the sovereign is only Yang Su.
translations.idiomatic: Yet deposition and installation are matters of state; only Yang Su can sway the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 移素謀者，唯其弟約。

translations.literal: The one who can move Su in plotting is only his younger brother Yue.
translations.idiomatic: And the one who can move Yang Su is only his younger brother Yue.

sentences.zh: 述雅知約，請朝京師，與約共圖廢立。」

translations.literal: Shu was on close terms with Yue; he asked to go to the capital and with Yue together plot deposition and establishment."
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu knew Yue well; he asked leave to go to the capital and plot the succession with him."

sentences.zh: 晉王大悅，多齎金寶，資述入關。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jin was greatly pleased and sent much gold and treasure to supply Shu entering the passes.
translations.idiomatic: The prince was delighted and loaded Wenshu with gold and jewels for his journey into the capital.

sentences.zh: 述數請約，盛陳器玩，與之酣暢，因共博戲，每陽不勝，輸所將金寶。

translations.literal: Shu repeatedly invited Yue, lavishly displayed vessels and curios, drank deeply with him, and then gambled together, each time feigning not to win and losing the gold and treasure he had brought.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu invited Yue again and again, displayed fine vessels and curios, drank with him until they were merry, then gambled—always pretending to lose and forfeiting the gold and jewels he had brought.

sentences.zh: 約所得既多，稍以謝述。

translations.literal: After Yue's gains were many, he gradually thanked Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yue had won heavily, he began to thank Wenshu in turn.

sentences.zh: 述因曰：「此晉王賜述，令與公為歡。」

translations.literal: Shu then said: "This is what the Prince of Jin bestowed on Shu, ordering me to share pleasure with you."
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu then said, "These were gifts from Prince Jin to me, meant for me to share pleasure with you."

sentences.zh: 約大驚曰：「何為者？」

translations.literal: Yue was greatly startled and said: "What is this for?"
translations.idiomatic: Yue was astonished. "What does this mean?"

sentences.zh: 述因為王申意。

translations.literal: Shu then conveyed the prince's intent on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu then laid out the prince's intentions.

sentences.zh: 約然其說，退言於素，亦從之。

translations.literal: Yue approved his argument, withdrew and spoke to Su, and Su also followed it.
translations.idiomatic: Yue accepted the plan, spoke to Yang Su, and Su agreed as well.

sentences.zh: 於是晉王與述情好益密，命述子士及尚南陽公主，後賞賜不可勝計。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Prince of Jin and Shu grew still closer in affection; he ordered Shu's son Shiji to marry the Princess of Nanyang, and afterward rewards and gifts were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: From then on prince and Wenshu drew still closer; the prince had Wenshu's son Shiji marry the Princess of Nanyang, and thereafter lavished rewards beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 及晉王為皇太子，以述為左衛率。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Jin became crown prince, he made Shu Left Guard Commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince became crown prince, he appointed Wenshu commander of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 舊令，率官第四品，以述素貴，遂進率品第三，其見重如此。

translations.literal: By old regulation the commander's office was fourth rank; because Shu had long been honored, his commander's rank was advanced to third—such was the weight in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: By regulation the guard commander's post was fourth rank, but because Wenshu had long been eminent his office was raised to third rank—such was the esteem in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 煬帝嗣位，拜左衛大將軍，參掌武官選事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang succeeded, he was appointed Left Guard Grand General and took part in managing selection of military officials.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, Wenshu was made Left Guard Grand General and helped manage appointments among military officers.

sentences.zh: 後改封許國公，尋加開府儀同三司，每冬正朝會，輒給鼓吹一部。

translations.literal: Later he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Xu, soon added Opening the Government with Protocol Equal to Three Offices, and every winter at the formal court assembly he was always given one set of martial music.
translations.idiomatic: He was later enfeoffed as Duke of Xu, soon granted the ceremonial rank of honorary commander with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, and at each winter court assembly was given a full ensemble of martial music.

sentences.zh: 從幸榆林，時鐵勒契弊歌稜攻敗吐谷渾。

translations.literal: Following the emperor on a visit to Yulin, at that time the Tiele chieftain Qibi Geleng attacked and defeated Tuyuhun.
translations.idiomatic: Accompanying the emperor to Yulin, he found the Tiele leader Qibi Geleng had just routed Tuyuhun.

sentences.zh: 其部攜散，遂遣使請降，求救。

translations.literal: His tribes scattered in flight, and he then sent envoys to request surrender and ask for rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Qibi's tribes scattered in flight, and he sent envoys to surrender and beg for aid.

sentences.zh: 帝令述以兵撫納降附。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered Shu to take troops to comfort and receive the surrendering and attaching.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Wenshu to take troops and receive the surrendering tribes.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾見述擁強兵，懼不敢降，遂西遁。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun saw Shu with strong troops, feared and dared not surrender, and then fled west.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing Wenshu at the head of a strong force, Tuyuhun dared not submit and fled west.

sentences.zh: 述追至曼頭城，攻拔之。

translations.literal: Shu pursued to Mantou City and stormed and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu pursued to Mantou City and stormed it.

sentences.zh: 乘勝至赤水城，復拔之。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory to Chishui City, he again stormed and took it.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing the victory to Chishui City, he took that as well.

sentences.zh: 其餘黨走屯丘尼川，進擊，大破之，獲其王公、尚書、將軍二百人。

translations.literal: The remaining factions fled and encamped at Qiuni River; he advanced and struck, greatly defeating them, and captured two hundred of their kings, dukes, ministers, and generals.
translations.idiomatic: The remnant bands fled to Qiuni River; he attacked and routed them, capturing two hundred of their princes, ministers, and generals.

sentences.zh: 渾主南走雪山，其故地皆空。

translations.literal: The Tuyuhun ruler fled south to Snow Mountain; his former lands were all empty.
translations.idiomatic: The Tuyuhun ruler fled south toward Snow Mountain, and his former lands lay empty.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 明年，從帝西巡至金山，登燕支，述每為斥候。

translations.literal: The next year, following the emperor on a western tour to Golden Mountain and ascending Yanzhi, Shu each time served as scout.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, on the western tour to Golden Mountain and the ascent of Yanzhi, Wenshu served repeatedly as advance scout.

sentences.zh: 時渾賊復寇張掖，述進擊走之。

translations.literal: At that time Tuyuhun bandits again raided Zhangye; Shu advanced and struck and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun raiders struck Zhangye again, Wenshu advanced and drove them off.

sentences.zh: 還至江都宮，敕述與蘇威常典選舉，參預朝政。

translations.literal: Returning to the Jiangdu Palace, the emperor ordered Shu and Su Wei regularly to preside over selections and take part in court government.
translations.idiomatic: Back at the Jiangdu Palace, the emperor ordered Wenshu and Su Wei to oversee selections regularly and join in governing.

sentences.zh: 述時貴重，委任與威等，其親愛則過之。

translations.literal: Shu at that time was noble and weighty; his commission was equal to Wei's, but in personal favor he surpassed him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu was then at the height of power, entrusted equally with Su Wei, yet favored even more warmly.

sentences.zh: 帝所得遠方貢獻及四時口味，輒見班賜，中使相望於道。

translations.literal: Whatever the emperor received in tribute from distant regions and seasonal delicacies, he would at once bestow on Shu; palace envoys lined the road in sight of one another.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute from distant lands and seasonal delicacies reached the emperor only to be passed on to Wenshu, palace envoys crowding the road in relays.

sentences.zh: 述善於供奉，俯仰折旋，容止便辟，宿衛咸取則焉。

translations.literal: Shu was skilled at attendance; in bowing and turning his bearing was nimble and obsequious, and the palace guards all took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at court service—every bow and turn graceful and obsequious—so that even the palace guards took him as their model.

sentences.zh: 又有巧思，凡所裝飾，皆出人意表。

translations.literal: He also had ingenious thought; whatever he adorned all exceeded people's expectations.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for design as well; whatever he arranged surprised everyone.

sentences.zh: 數以奇服異物進宮掖，由是帝彌悅焉。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presented strange garments and exotic objects to the inner palace, and thereby the emperor was still more pleased.
translations.idiomatic: He often sent outlandish garments and curios to the inner palace, and the emperor grew still fonder of him.

sentences.zh: 言無不從，勢傾朝廷。

translations.literal: No word of his went unheeded; his power leaned on the court.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing he said went unheeded; his power overshadowed the court.

sentences.zh: 左衛將軍張瑾與述連官，嘗有評議，偶不中意，述張目瞋之，瑾惶懼而走。

translations.literal: Left Guard General Zhang Jin was consecutive in office with Shu; they once had a discussion, and by chance it did not please him—Shu widened his eyes and glared, and Jin in fear and alarm fled.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard General Zhang Jin served in the same office and once debated a point with Wenshu. When Wenshu took offense he glared, and Zhang fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 文武百僚莫敢違忤。

translations.literal: Among civil and military officials of every rank none dared oppose him.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials alike dared not cross him.

sentences.zh: 性貪鄙，知人有珍異物，必求取，富商大賈及隴右諸胡子弟，皆接以恩意，呼之為兒。

translations.literal: His nature was greedy and base; if he knew someone had rare treasures he was sure to seek them, and great merchants and the sons of Hu families west of Long all he received with gracious intent, calling them "son."
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and base by nature, he seized on anyone known to possess rarities; rich merchants and the sons of frontier Hu families he courted as "sons."

sentences.zh: 由是競加饋遺，金寶累積。

translations.literal: Thereby they vied to add gifts, and gold and jewels piled up.
translations.idiomatic: They vied to shower him with gifts until gold and jewels piled high.

sentences.zh: 後庭曳羅綺者甚眾，家僮千餘人，皆控良馬，被服金玉。

translations.literal: In the rear court many trailed silk and brocade; household servants numbered more than a thousand, all riding fine horses and clad in gold and jade.
translations.idiomatic: His rear court swarmed with women in silk and brocade; more than a thousand household servants rode fine horses clad in gold and jade.

sentences.zh: 及征高麗，述為扶餘道軍將，臨發，帝謂曰：「禮，七十者行役以婦人從，公宜以家累自隨。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Goguryeo came, Shu was army commander of the Fuyu route; on the eve of departure the emperor said to him: "By ritual, when one of seventy goes on campaign women may follow; you, sir, ought to bring your household dependents yourself.
translations.idiomatic: On the Goguryeo campaign Wenshu commanded the Fuyu route army. Before he marched the emperor told him, "Ritual allows a man of seventy to take his women on campaign—you should bring your household along.

sentences.zh: 古稱婦人不入軍，謂臨戰時耳。

translations.literal: The ancients said women do not enter the army—this refers only to the moment of battle.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said women do not enter the army, but they meant only at the moment of battle.

sentences.zh: 至軍壘間，無所傷也。

translations.literal: Within the army camps there is no harm.
translations.idiomatic: In camp there is no harm in it.

sentences.zh: 項籍虞兮，即其故事。」

translations.literal: Xiang Yu and Yu Ji are exactly that precedent."
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Yu and Lady Yu are the very precedent."

sentences.zh: 述與九軍至鴨綠水，糧盡，議欲班師。

translations.literal: Shu with the nine armies reached the Yalu River; provisions were exhausted and they discussed wanting to withdraw the army.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu led the nine armies to the Yalu. Provisions ran out and the commanders debated withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 諸將多異同，述又不測帝意。

translations.literal: The generals mostly differed in agreement and opposition, and Shu also could not fathom the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: The generals were divided, and Wenshu could not read the emperor's mind.

sentences.zh: 會乙支文德來詣其營，述先與于仲文俱奉密旨，令誘執文德。

translations.literal: It happened that Ye Zhiven came to visit his camp; Shu earlier with Yu Zhongwen together had received a secret order to lure and seize Wen De.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Zhiven came to his camp. Wenshu and Yu Zhongwen had earlier received secret orders to lure and seize him.

sentences.zh: 既而緩縱，文德逃歸，述內不自安，遂與諸將度水追之。

translations.literal: Afterward they slackened restraint; Wen De escaped and returned, and Shu inwardly was ill at ease, so he with the generals crossed the water in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: They hesitated; Wen De escaped. Uneasy within, Wenshu crossed the river in pursuit with the other generals.

sentences.zh: 時文德見述軍中多饑色，欲疲述眾，每鬥便北。

translations.literal: At that time Wen De saw many signs of hunger in Shu's army and wished to weary Shu's masses; each time they fought he at once turned north.
translations.idiomatic: Wen De saw hunger in the army and meant to wear them down, feigning retreat whenever they fought.

sentences.zh: 述一日中七戰皆捷，既恃驟勝，又內逼群議，遂進，東濟薩水，去平壤城三十里，因山為營。

translations.literal: Shu in one day fought seven battles and all were victories; trusting in sudden victory and inwardly pressed by the crowd of opinions, he then advanced, crossed east over the Saba River, was thirty li from Pyongyang city, and made camp relying on the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu won seven battles in a single day. Trusting in swift victory and pressed by his officers, he advanced, crossed the Saba eastward, camped thirty li from Pyongyang against the hills.

sentences.zh: 文德復遣使偽降，請述曰：「若旋師者，當奉高元朝行在所。」

translations.literal: Wen De again sent envoys in false surrender and requested of Shu: "If you turn the army, I shall present King Gao Yuan at the traveling palace."
translations.idiomatic: Wen De sent envoys feigning surrender, saying, "If Wenshu withdraws, I will deliver King Gao Yuan to the imperial camp."

sentences.zh: 述見士卒疲弊，不可復戰，又平壤險固，卒難致力，遂因其詐而還。

translations.literal: Shu saw the soldiers weary and spent, unable to fight again, and Pyongyang perilous and solid, hard to exert force against in the end, so he followed their deceit and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his troops exhausted and Pyongyang too strong to storm, Wenshu took the ruse for truth and turned back.

sentences.zh: 眾半濟，賊擊後軍。

translations.literal: When the masses were half across, the bandits struck the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: Halfway across the river the enemy struck the rear.

sentences.zh: 於是大潰不可禁止，九軍敗績，一日一夜，還至鴨綠水，行四百五十里。

translations.literal: Thereupon there was great rout that could not be stopped; the nine armies were defeated, and in one day and one night they returned to the Yalu River, traveling four hundred fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: The army collapsed beyond control. The nine armies were ruined; in a day and a night they fled four hundred fifty li back to the Yalu.

sentences.zh: 初度遼，九軍三十萬五千人，及還至遼東城，唯二千七百人。

translations.literal: At first when crossing Liao there were three hundred five thousand men in the nine armies; when they returned to Liaodong city only two thousand seven hundred men remained.
translations.idiomatic: Three hundred five thousand had crossed the Liao; only twenty-seven hundred returned to Liaodong.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，除其名。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and struck his name from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor in anger struck his name from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝又事遼東，復述官爵，待之如初。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor again undertook Liaodong affairs, restored Shu's office and titles, and treated him as at first.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, campaigning in Liaodong again, the emperor restored his titles and treated him as before.

sentences.zh: 從至遼東，與將軍楊義臣率兵復臨鴨綠水。

translations.literal: Following to Liaodong, with General Yang Yichen he led troops again to come before the Yalu River.
translations.idiomatic: He followed to Liaodong and with Yang Yichen again brought the army to the Yalu.

sentences.zh: 會楊玄感作亂，帝召述馳驛討玄感。

translations.literal: It happened that Yang Xuangan raised rebellion; the emperor summoned Shu to ride post-horses and suppress Xuangan.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xuangan rebelled; the emperor summoned Wenshu to ride post relays and crush him.

sentences.zh: 時玄感逼東都，聞述軍至，西遁將圖關中。

translations.literal: At that time Xuangan pressed the Eastern Capital; hearing Shu's army had arrived, he fled west intending to scheme for Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Xuangan was pressing the Eastern Capital; hearing Wenshu was coming, he fled west toward Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 述與刑部尚書衛玄、右驍衛大將軍來護兒、武衛將軍屈突通等躡之。

translations.literal: Shu with Minister of Justice Wei Xuan, Right Valiant Cavalry Guard Grand General Lai Huer, Martial Guard General Qutu Tong, and others followed on his heels.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu pursued with Wei Xuan, Lai Huer, Qutu Tong, and others.

sentences.zh: 至閿鄉皇天原，與玄感相及，斬其首，傳行在所。

translations.literal: Reaching Huangtian Plain in Wenxiang, they caught Xuangan, beheaded him, and sent the head to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangtian Plain in Wenxiang they overtook him, took his head, and sent it to the emperor's camp.

sentences.zh: 復從東征，至懷遠而還。

translations.literal: He again followed the eastern campaign, reaching Huaiyuan and returning.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the eastern campaign again as far as Huaiyuan and returned.

sentences.zh: 突厥之圍雁門也，帝大懼，述請潰圍而出。

translations.literal: When the Turks besieged Yanmen, the emperor was greatly afraid; Shu requested to break the encirclement and go out.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks besieged Yanmen the emperor was terrified; Wenshu urged breaking out of the encirclement.

sentences.zh: 來護兒及樊子蓋並固諫，帝乃止。

translations.literal: Lai Huer and Fan Zigai together firmly remonstrated, and the emperor then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Lai Huer and Fan Zigai strongly dissuaded him, and the emperor held back.

sentences.zh: 及圍解，次太原，議者多勸帝還京師，帝有難色。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted they halted at Taiyuan; many in council urged the emperor to return to the capital, and the emperor showed a troubled countenance.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege lifted they halted at Taiyuan. Many urged a return to the capital, but the emperor looked troubled.

sentences.zh: 述奏曰：「從官妻子多在東都，請便道向洛陽，自潼關入。」

translations.literal: Shu memorialized saying: "The followers' and officials' wives and children are mostly in the Eastern Capital; I request taking the convenient route toward Luoyang and entering by Tong Pass."
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu memorialized, "Your attendants' families are mostly in the Eastern Capital. Take the direct road to Luoyang and enter through Tong Pass."

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 尋至東都，又觀望帝意，勸幸江都宮。

translations.literal: Soon they reached the Eastern Capital; again watching the emperor's intent, he urged visiting the Jiangdu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after reaching the Eastern Capital he read the emperor's mood and urged the tour to the Jiangdu Palace.

sentences.zh: 述于江都遇疾，及疾篤，帝令中使相望於第，謂述有何言。

translations.literal: Wenshu fell ill at Jiangdu, and when the illness became grave, the emperor sent palace envoys one after another to his residence to ask whether Wenshu had anything to say.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu fell ill at Jiangdu. When his illness became grave, the emperor sent palace envoys in succession to his residence to ask whether he had anything to say.

sentences.zh: 述曰：「願陛下一能降臨。」

translations.literal: Wenshu said, “I wish that Your Majesty might once be able to descend and visit.”
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu said, “I only wish Your Majesty might come once in person.”

sentences.zh: 帝遣司宮魏氏謂曰：「公危篤，朕憚相煩動。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Lady Wei of the Palace Service to tell him, “You are critically ill, and I am reluctant to trouble you by making you move.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Lady Wei of the Palace Service to say, “You are critically ill, and I hesitate to trouble you by making you stir.

sentences.zh: 必有言，可陳也。」

translations.literal: If you truly have something to say, you may state it.”
translations.idiomatic: If you truly have something to say, you may state it.”

sentences.zh: 述流涕曰：「臣子化及，早預籓邸，願陛下哀憐之。

translations.literal: Wenshu shed tears and said, “My son Huaji early entered service in Your Highness’s princely household; I beg Your Majesty to pity him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu wept and said, “My son Huaji served early in Your Majesty’s princely household. I beg Your Majesty to show him compassion.

sentences.zh: 士及夙蒙天恩，亦堪驅策。

translations.literal: Shiji has long received heavenly favor and is also fit to be driven in service.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji has long received imperial favor and is also fit to be employed.

sentences.zh: 臣死後，智及不可久留，願早除之，望不破門戶。」

translations.literal: After I die, Zhiji must not be kept long; I hope he will be removed early, and hope that he will not ruin the household.”
translations.idiomatic: After I die, Zhiji must not be kept long. I hope he will be removed early, so that he does not ruin the household.”

sentences.zh: 魏氏返命，隱其言，因詭對曰：「述唯憶陛下耳。」

translations.literal: Lady Wei returned with her report, concealed his words, and deceitfully replied, “Wenshu only remembers Your Majesty.”
translations.idiomatic: Lady Wei returned with the message, concealed what he had said, and falsely replied, “Wenshu only thinks of Your Majesty.”

sentences.zh: 帝泫然曰：「述憶我耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor, with tears about to fall, said, “Does Wenshu remember me?”
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, moved to tears, said, “Does Wenshu think of me?”

sentences.zh: 將親臨之，宮人百僚諫乃止。

translations.literal: He was about to visit him personally, but the palace attendants and hundred officials remonstrated, and only then did he stop.
translations.idiomatic: He was about to go in person, but palace attendants and officials remonstrated, and he stopped.

sentences.zh: 及薨，帝為廢朝，贈司徒、尚書令、十郡太守，班劍四十人，轀輬車，前後部鼓吹，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: When Wenshu died, the emperor suspended court for him and posthumously granted him Minister over the Masses, Director of the Secretariat, Administrator of Ten Commanderies, forty honor guards with swords, a hearse, and front and rear bands of drums and pipes; his posthumous name was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenshu died, the emperor suspended court for him and posthumously honored him as Minister over the Masses, Director of the Secretariat, and Administrator of Ten Commanderies, with forty sword-bearing guards, a hearse, and front and rear processional bands; his posthumous name was Gong.

sentences.zh: 詔黃門侍郎裴矩祭乙太牢，鴻臚監護喪事。

translations.literal: He ordered Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Pei Ju to sacrifice with the second-grade grand offering, and the Chamberlain for Dependencies to supervise the funeral affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate Pei Ju to perform the sacrifice with a second-grade grand offering, while the Chamberlain for Dependencies supervised the funeral.

sentences.zh: 雲定興者，附會於述。

translations.literal: Yun Dingxing was one who attached himself to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Dingxing was a man who curried favor with Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 初，定興女為皇太子勇昭訓，及勇廢，除名配少府。

translations.literal: At first Dingxing's daughter was Crown Prince Yong's Lady Zhaoxun; when Yong was deposed she was struck from the rolls and assigned to the Palace Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter had been Lady Zhaoxun to Crown Prince Yong; when Yong was deposed she was struck from the rolls and sent to the Palace Workshop.

sentences.zh: 定興先得昭訓明珠絡帷，私賂於述，自是數共交遊。

translations.literal: Dingxing had earlier obtained Lady Zhaoxun's pearl-net curtain and privately bribed Shu with it; from then on they often associated together.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing had obtained her pearl-net curtain and secretly bribed Wenshu with it; thereafter they often kept company.

sentences.zh: 定興每時節必有賂遺，並以音樂幹述。

translations.literal: Dingxing at every season was sure to have bribes and gifts, and also used music to seek favor with Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Every season brought gifts, and he also used music to win Wenshu's favor.

sentences.zh: 述素好著奇服，炫耀時人。

translations.literal: Shu had long loved wearing strange garments and dazzling the men of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu had always loved outlandish dress and dazzling the fashionable.

sentences.zh: 定興為制馬韉，於後角上缺方三寸，以露白色，世輕薄者率仿學之，謂為許公缺勢。

translations.literal: Dingxing made for him a horse saddle-cloth with a square three inches missing on the rear corner to expose white; the frivolous of the age mostly imitated and learned it, calling it Duke Xu's missing corner.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing made him a saddlecloth with a three-inch square cut from the rear corner to show white lining; fops copied it and called it the Duke of Xu's gap.

sentences.zh: 又遇天寒，定興曰：「入內宿衛，必當耳冷。」

translations.literal: Again when the weather was cold Dingxing said: "Entering the palace for night guard, the ears must surely be cold."
translations.idiomatic: One cold day Dingxing said, "On night duty inside the palace your ears must freeze."

sentences.zh: 述曰：「然。」

translations.literal: Shu said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu said, "True."

sentences.zh: 乃制夾頭巾，令深袹耳，人又學之，名為許公袹勢。

translations.literal: Then he made a wrapped head-cloth, ordering it deep to wrap the ears; people again imitated it, naming it Duke Xu's wrap.
translations.idiomatic: He had a wrapped headcloth made deep enough to cover the ears; imitators called it the Duke of Xu's wrap.

sentences.zh: 述大悅曰：「雲兄所作，必能變俗。

translations.literal: Shu was greatly pleased and said: "What Brother Yun makes is sure to change custom.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu was delighted. "Brother Yun's inventions are sure to change fashion.

sentences.zh: 我聞作事可法，故不虛也。」

translations.literal: I have heard that what one does can serve as a model, so it is not empty."
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that what one does can set an example—so this is no empty boast."

sentences.zh: 後帝將事四夷，大造兵器，述薦之，因敕少府工匠並取其節度。

translations.literal: Later when the emperor was about to undertake affairs with the four barbarians and greatly made weapons, Shu recommended him, and therefore ordered the Palace Workshop craftsmen all to take his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the emperor prepared campaigns against the four quarters and ordered vast armaments, Wenshu recommended him and put all Palace Workshop craftsmen under his direction.

sentences.zh: 述欲為之求官，謂之曰：「兄所制器仗併合上心，而不得官者，為長寧兄弟猶未死耳。」

translations.literal: Shu wished to seek office for him and said to him: "The arms and gear you, brother, make all suit the sovereign's mind, yet you cannot obtain office because the Changning brothers are still not dead."
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu wanted an office for him and said, "Your arms and gear suit the emperor perfectly, yet you cannot rise while the Changning brothers still live."

sentences.zh: 定興曰：「此無用物，何不勸上殺之？」

translations.literal: Dingxing said: "These are useless men—why not urge the sovereign to kill them?"
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing said, "They are useless—why not urge the emperor to kill them?"

sentences.zh: 述因奏曰：「房陵諸子，年並成立，今欲動兵征討，若將從駕，則守掌為難；

translations.literal: Shu then memorialized saying: "The sons of Fangling are all grown; now when we wish to move troops on campaign, if they follow the imperial carriage, guarding and holding will be difficult;
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu memorialized, "The sons of Fangling are grown. If they follow the campaign train, guarding them will be hard;

sentences.zh: 若留一處，又恐不可。

translations.literal: if one is left in one place, again we fear it may not do.
translations.idiomatic: if one is left behind, that too is dangerous.

sentences.zh: 進退無用，請早處分。」

translations.literal: Advancing and retreating they are useless—please dispose of them early."
translations.idiomatic: They are useless either way—dispose of them soon."

sentences.zh: 因鳩殺長寧，又遣以下七弟分配嶺表，于路盡殺之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he poisoned Changning, and again sent the seven younger brothers below him to be assigned across the Ling ranges, and on the road killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: He poisoned Changning and sent the seven younger brothers into exile beyond the Ling ranges, killing them all on the road.

sentences.zh: 其年大閱，帝稱甲仗為佳，述奏並雲定興之功也。

translations.literal: That year at the great review the emperor praised the armor and weapons as excellent; Shu memorialized that it was all Yun Dingxing's merit.
translations.idiomatic: At the grand review that year the emperor praised the armor; Wenshu credited Yun Dingxing.

sentences.zh: 擢授少府丞。

translations.literal: He was promoted and appointed Assistant Director of the Palace Workshop.
translations.idiomatic: Dingxing was promoted to assistant director of the Palace Workshop.

sentences.zh: 十一年，累遷屯衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted in succession to Grand General of the Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven he rose to grand general of the Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 又有趙行樞者，本太常樂戶，家財億計。

translations.literal: There was also Zhao Xingshu, originally a music-house man of the Grand Imperial Sacrifices, with household wealth reckoned in the hundreds of millions.
translations.idiomatic: There was also Zhao Xingshu, once a musician of the Grand Sacrifices office, whose household wealth ran to hundreds of millions.

sentences.zh: 述謂為兒，受其賂遺，稱為驍勇，起家為折沖郎將。

translations.literal: Shu called him "son," received his bribes and gifts, and praised him as fierce and brave, beginning his career as Colonel of the Rapid Response.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu called him "son," took his bribes, praised his valor, and had him made a rapid-response colonel.

sentences.zh: 化及，述長子也。

translations.literal: Huaji was Wenshu’s eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was Wenshu’s eldest son.

sentences.zh: 性凶險，不循法度，好乘肥挾彈，馳鶩道中，由是長安謂之輕薄公子。

translations.literal: His nature was vicious and dangerous, and he did not follow laws and regulations; he liked to ride fine horses carrying a pellet-bow and gallop along the roads, and because of this Chang’an called him a frivolous young lord.
translations.idiomatic: He was vicious and dangerous by nature and ignored the law. He liked riding fine horses with a pellet-bow at his side, galloping through the streets, so Chang’an called him a frivolous young noble.

sentences.zh: 煬帝為太子時，常領千牛出入臥內。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang was crown prince, Huaji regularly commanded the Qianniu guards and entered and exited the inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was crown prince, Huaji regularly commanded the Qianniu guards and had access to the inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 累遷至太子僕，以受納貨賄，再三免官。

translations.literal: Through successive promotions he reached Supervisor of the Crown Prince’s Stables, but because he accepted goods and bribes, he was dismissed from office repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: After repeated promotions he reached Supervisor of the Crown Prince’s Stables, but was dismissed again and again for taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 太子嬖昵之。

translations.literal: The crown prince favored and was intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince was fond of him and kept him close.

sentences.zh: 俄而復職，又以其弟士及尚南陽公主。

translations.literal: Soon he was restored to office, and moreover his younger brother Shiji married Princess Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was restored to office, and his younger brother Shiji married Princess Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 由此益驕，處公卿間，言辭不遜，多所淩轢。

translations.literal: Because of this he became still more arrogant; among dukes and ministers his speech was disrespectful and he often bullied others.
translations.idiomatic: This made him still more arrogant. Among the high ministers his speech was insolent, and he often bullied people.

sentences.zh: 見人子女狗馬珍玩，必請托求之。

translations.literal: When he saw others’ sons and daughters, dogs and horses, or precious playthings, he would always ask intermediaries to request them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he saw someone’s sons or daughters, dogs or horses, or rare playthings, he would use connections to ask for them.

sentences.zh: 常與屠販者遊，以規其利。

translations.literal: He often associated with butchers and peddlers in order to scheme for their profits.
translations.idiomatic: He often consorted with butchers and peddlers, scheming to profit from them.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，拜太僕少卿，益恃舊恩，貪冒尤甚。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang ascended the throne, Huaji was appointed Junior Chamberlain of the Imperial Stables; he relied even more on old favor, and his greed and recklessness became especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Yang took the throne, Huaji was appointed Junior Chamberlain of the Imperial Stables. Relying still more on old favor, he became especially greedy and reckless.

sentences.zh: 煬帝幸榆林，化及與弟智及違禁與突厥交市。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang visited Yulin, Huaji and his younger brother Zhiji violated the prohibition by trading with the Turks.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang visited Yulin, Huaji and his younger brother Zhiji violated the ban and traded with the Turks.

sentences.zh: 帝大怒，囚之數月。

translations.literal: The emperor was furious and imprisoned them for several months.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and imprisoned them for several months.

sentences.zh: 還京師，欲斬之而後入城，解衣辮髪訖，以主救之，乃釋，並智及並賜述為奴。

translations.literal: On returning to the capital, he intended to behead them before entering the city; after their clothes had been stripped and their hair braided, because the princess rescued them, they were released, and both Huaji and Zhiji were given to Wenshu as slaves.
translations.idiomatic: On returning to the capital, the emperor meant to behead them before entering the city. Their clothes had been stripped and their hair braided, but the princess interceded, so they were released; Huaji and Zhiji were both given to Wenshu as slaves.

sentences.zh: 述薨後，煬帝追憶之，起化及為右屯衛將軍，將作少監。

translations.literal: After Wenshu died, Emperor Yang remembered him and raised Huaji to be General of the Right Garrison Guard and Junior Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: After Wenshu’s death, Emperor Yang remembered him and appointed Huaji General of the Right Garrison Guard and Junior Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 時李密據洛口，煬帝懼，留淮左，不敢還都。

translations.literal: At that time Li Mi held Luokou; Emperor Yang was afraid, remained on the Huai region's left bank, and dared not return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi held Luokou; Emperor Yang, afraid, lingered south of the Huai and dared not return north.

sentences.zh: 從駕驍果多關中人，久客羈旅，見帝無西還意，謀欲叛歸。

translations.literal: The valiant guards following the carriage were mostly men of Guanzhong; long guests on distant journeys, they saw the emperor had no intent to return west and plotted to rebel and go home.
translations.idiomatic: Many valiant guards following the emperor were Guanzhong men. Long away from home, seeing no sign the emperor would return west, they plotted to desert.

sentences.zh: 時武賁郎將司馬德戡總領驍果，屯於東城，風聞兵士欲叛，未審，遣校尉元武達陰問知情，因謀構逆。

translations.literal: At that time Martial Guard General Sima Dekan commanded the valiant guards, encamped in the eastern city; hearing rumors the soldiers wished to rebel but not yet verifying, he sent Colonel Yuan Wuda secretly to ask who knew, and thereby plotted treason.
translations.idiomatic: Martial Guard General Sima Dekan commanded the valiant guards in the eastern city. Hearing rumors of mutiny, he sent Colonel Yuan Wuda to probe, then plotted treason.

sentences.zh: 共所善武賁郎將元禮、直閣裴虔通互相扇惑曰：「聞陛下欲築宮丹陽，人人並謀逃去。

translations.literal: Together with their close associates Martial Guard General Yuan Li and Direct Attendant Pei Qiantong they mutually incited one another, saying: "We hear the sovereign intends to build a palace at Danyang; everyone alike plots to flee.
translations.idiomatic: With his confederates Yuan Li and Pei Qiantong he whispered, "We hear the emperor will build a palace at Danyang—every man plans to run.

sentences.zh: 我欲言之，恐先事見誅。

translations.literal: I wish to speak of it but fear being killed first for foreknowledge.
translations.idiomatic: If I speak first I may be killed for foreknowledge.

sentences.zh: 今知而不言，後事發當族，將如之何？」

translations.literal: Now if I know and do not speak, when the matter breaks out later my clan will be exterminated—what then shall we do?"
translations.idiomatic: Yet if I know and stay silent, when it breaks out my clan dies—what then?"

sentences.zh: 虔通曰：「主上實爾。」

translations.literal: Qiantong said: "The sovereign is truly so."
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong said, "The emperor truly means it."

sentences.zh: 德戡又謂兩人曰：「我聞關中陷沒，李孝常以華陰叛，陛下囚其二弟，將盡殺之。

translations.literal: Dekan again said to the two: "I hear Guanzhong has fallen; Li Xiaochang rebelled at Huayin, and the sovereign imprisoned his two younger brothers and will kill them all.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan added, "Guanzhong has fallen; Li Xiaochang rebelled at Huayin. The emperor imprisoned his brothers and will kill them all.

sentences.zh: 吾輩家屬在西安，得無此慮？」

translations.literal: Our families are in Xi'an—can we be without this worry?"
translations.idiomatic: Our families are in Xi'an—can we not fear the same?"

sentences.zh: 虔通等曰：「正恐旦暮及誅，計無所出。」

translations.literal: Qiantong and the others said: "We truly fear execution morning or evening; there is no plan."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "We fear execution any day—there is no plan."

sentences.zh: 德戡曰：「驍果若走，可與俱去。」

translations.literal: Dekan said: "If the valiant guards flee, we can go with them."
translations.idiomatic: Dekan said, "If the guards flee, we flee with them."

sentences.zh: 虔通等曰：「誠如公言。」

translations.literal: Qiantong and the others said: "It is truly as you say."
translations.idiomatic: They said, "It is truly as you say."

sentences.zh: 因遞相招誘。

translations.literal: Thereupon they in turn invited and enticed one another.
translations.idiomatic: They began recruiting one another.

sentences.zh: 又轉告內史舍人元敏、鷹揚郎將孟景、符璽郎牛方裕，直長許弘仁、薛世良、城門郎唐奉義、醫正張愷等，日夜聚博，約為刎頸交，言無回避，於坐中輒論叛計，並相然許。

translations.literal: They again told Imperial Secretariat Aide Yuan Min, Hawkish Guard General Meng Jing, Seal Keeper Niu Fangyu, Direct Chief Xu Hongren, Xue Shiliang, Gate Officer Tang Fengyi, Court Physician Zhang Kai, and others; day and night they gathered to gamble, pledged throat-cutting friendship, spoke without reserve, and at the seat often discussed rebel plans, all approving one another.
translations.idiomatic: They drew in Yuan Min, Meng Jing, Niu Fangyu, Xu Hongren, Xue Shiliang, Tang Fengyi, Zhang Kai, and others—gambling nightly, swearing blood brotherhood, debating rebellion openly.

sentences.zh: 時李質在禁，令驍果守之，中外交通，所謀益急。

translations.literal: At that time Li Zhi was in confinement and ordered the valiant guards to guard him; inside and outside communicated, and the plot grew more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhi was imprisoned under guard by the valiant guards; inside and outside the plot linked up and urgency grew.

sentences.zh: 又趙行樞先交智及；

translations.literal: Zhao Xingshu had earlier befriended Zhi Ji;
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xingshu was already close to Yu Zhi Ji;

sentences.zh: 勳侍楊士覽者，宇文氏之甥。

translations.literal: Meritorious Attendant Yang Shiguan was a nephew of the Yuwen clan.
translations.idiomatic: Meritorious Attendant Yang Shiguan was a Yuwen nephew.

sentences.zh: 二人同以告智及。

translations.literal: The two together told Zhi Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Both told Zhi Ji.

sentences.zh: 智及素狂勃，聞之喜，即共見德戡，期以三月十五日舉兵同叛，劫十二衛武馬，虜掠居人財物西歸。

translations.literal: Zhi Ji was by nature wild and overbearing; hearing it he was pleased, and at once together saw Dekan, fixing the fifteenth day of the third month to raise troops in common rebellion, seize the twelve guards' martial horses, and plunder residents' goods to return west.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Ji was rash and violent; delighted, he met Dekan and set the fifteenth of the third month to rebel, seize the twelve guards' horses, and plunder westward.

sentences.zh: 智及曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhi Ji said: "It is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Ji said, "No.

sentences.zh: 今天實喪隋，英雄並起，因行大事，此帝王業也。」

translations.literal: Heaven today has lost Sui; heroes rise together—take this chance for a great deed; this is an emperor's enterprise."
translations.idiomatic: Heaven has abandoned Sui; heroes rise—seize the moment. This is an emperor's venture."

sentences.zh: 德戡然之。

translations.literal: Dekan approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan agreed.

sentences.zh: 行樞、世良請以化及為主，約定，方告化及。

translations.literal: Xingshu and Shiliang asked to make Huaji the leader; when the agreement was fixed, only then did they tell Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Xingshu and Shiliang proposed Huaji as leader; only when all agreed did they tell him.

sentences.zh: 化及性駑怯，初聞之，大懼，色動流汗，久之乃定。

translations.literal: Huaji's nature was dull and timid; at first hearing he was greatly afraid, his color moved and sweat flowed; only after long time did he settle.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji was dull and timid; at first he turned pale and sweated; only slowly did he steady himself.

sentences.zh: 義寧二年三月一日，德戡欲告眾人，恐心未一，更譎詐以脅驍果，謂許弘仁、張愷曰：「君是良醫，國家所使，出言惑眾，眾必信。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yining, on the first day of the third month, Dekan wished to tell the masses but feared hearts were not one; he again used deceit to threaten the valiant guards, telling Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai: "You are good physicians whom the state employs; words that delude the masses they are sure to believe.
translations.idiomatic: On the first day of the third month, second year of Yining, Dekan feared the men were not united and tricked the guards, telling Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai, "You are trusted physicians—your words will be believed.

sentences.zh: 君可入備身府，遍告所識者，言陛下聞驍果欲叛，多醖毒酒，因享會，盡鳩殺之，獨與南人留此。

translations.literal: You can enter the Personal Guard Office and everywhere tell those you know that the sovereign heard the valiant guards wished to rebel, brewed much poisoned wine, and at a feast will poison-kill them all, keeping only the southerners here.
translations.idiomatic: Tell everyone the emperor heard the guards would rebel, brewed poisoned wine, and will poison them at a feast, keeping only southerners.

sentences.zh: 群情必駭，因而舉事，無不諧矣。」

translations.literal: The crowd's feelings will surely be alarmed, and thereby raising the affair, nothing will fail to harmonize."
translations.idiomatic: Panic will spread—and the plot will succeed."

sentences.zh: 其月五日，弘仁等宣佈此言，驍果遞相告，謀反逾急。

translations.literal: On the fifth day of that month Hongren and the others proclaimed this speech; the valiant guards told one another in turn, and the plot to rebel grew more urgent.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifth Hongren spread the tale; the guards whispered to one another and mutiny neared.

sentences.zh: 德戡等知計行，遂以十日總召故人，諭以所為。

translations.literal: Dekan and the others knew the plan would proceed, so on the tenth they altogether summoned old friends and instructed them in what was to be done.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the moment had come, on the tenth Dekan summoned his circle and told them the plan.

sentences.zh: 眾皆伏曰：「唯將軍命！」

translations.literal: The masses all bowed and said: "Only the general's command!"
translations.idiomatic: All bowed and said, "We obey the general!"

sentences.zh: 其夜，奉義主閉城門，門皆不下鑰，至夜三更。

translations.literal: That night Fengyi presided over closing the city gates; the gates all had no locks set down, until the third watch of night.
translations.idiomatic: That night Tang Fengyi kept the gates unbarred until the third watch.

sentences.zh: 德戡於東城內集兵，得數萬人，舉火與城外相應。

translations.literal: Dekan within the eastern city gathered troops, obtaining several tens of thousands; they raised fires to correspond with those outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan mustered tens of thousands in the eastern city and lit signal fires matching those outside.

sentences.zh: 帝聞有聲，問是何事。

translations.literal: The emperor heard sounds and asked what affair it was.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard noise and asked what was happening.

sentences.zh: 虔通偽曰：「草坊被燒，外人救火，故喧囂耳。」

translations.literal: Qiantong falsely said: "The grass workshops are burning; outsiders are fighting the fire, hence the clamor."
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong lied, "Grass workshops are burning—men are fighting the fire, that is all the noise."

sentences.zh: 中外隔絕，帝以為然。

translations.literal: Inside and outside were cut off; the emperor believed it.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from outside, the emperor believed him.

sentences.zh: 孟景、智及於城外得千餘人，劫候衛武賁馮普樂，共布兵捉郭下街巷。

translations.literal: Meng Jing and Zhi Ji outside the city obtained more than a thousand men, seized and waited upon Martial Guard Feng Pule, and together deployed troops to seize the streets below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jing and Zhi Ji outside gathered a thousand men, seized Feng Pule, and seized the streets below the wall.

sentences.zh: 至五更，德戡授虔通兵，以換諸門衛士。

translations.literal: At the fifth watch Dekan gave Qiantong troops to replace the gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth watch Dekan gave Qiantong troops to replace the gate guards.

sentences.zh: 虔通因自開門，領數百騎，至成象殿，殺將軍獨孤盛。

translations.literal: Qiantong thereby himself opened the gate, leading several hundred horsemen to the Hall of Completed Images, and killed General Dugu Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong opened the gate himself, led hundreds of horsemen to the Hall of Completed Images, and killed General Dugu Sheng.

sentences.zh: 武賁郎將元禮遂引兵進。

translations.literal: Martial Guard Yuan Li then led troops forward.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Li advanced with his troops.

sentences.zh: 宿衛者皆走。

translations.literal: The night guards all fled.
translations.idiomatic: The night guards fled.

sentences.zh: 虔通進兵排左閤，馳入永巷問：「陛下安在？」

translations.literal: Qiantong advanced troops arrayed at the left wing, galloped into the Eternal Lane and asked: "Where is the sovereign?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong drove into the Eternal Lane and cried, "Where is His Majesty?"

sentences.zh: 有美人出房，指云：「在西閤。」

translations.literal: A beauty came out of a room and pointed, saying: "In the western wing."
translations.idiomatic: A palace woman pointed and said, "In the western wing."

sentences.zh: 從往執帝。

translations.literal: They went and seized the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝謂虔通曰：「卿非我故人乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said to Qiantong: "Are you not my old acquaintance!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Are you not my old friend!

sentences.zh: 何恨而反？」

translations.literal: What hatred makes you rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: What grudge drives you to rebel?"

sentences.zh: 虔通曰：「臣不敢反，但將士思歸，奉陛下還京師耳。」

translations.literal: Qiantong said: "Your servant dares not rebel, but the soldiers long to return home and escort Your Majesty back to the capital—that is all."
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong said, "I dare not rebel—the soldiers long for home and would escort Your Majesty to the capital, that is all."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「即為汝歸。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "I will at once return for you."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I will return at once for you."

sentences.zh: 虔通自勒兵守之。

translations.literal: Qiantong himself restrained troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantong kept troops guarding him.

sentences.zh: 至旦，孟景以甲騎迎化及。

translations.literal: At dawn Meng Jing with armored horsemen welcomed Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Meng Jing met Huaji with armored cavalry.

sentences.zh: 化及未知事果，戰慄不能言，人有謁之，但低頭據案，答曰「罪過」。

translations.literal: Huaji did not yet know whether the affair had succeeded; he trembled and could not speak; when someone called on him he only bowed his head over the desk and answered "guilt."
translations.idiomatic: Huaji did not yet know the coup had succeeded; he trembled and could not speak; to visitors he only bowed over his desk and muttered "guilt."

sentences.zh: 時士及在公主第，弗之知也。

translations.literal: At that time Shiji was at the princess's residence and did not know of it.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji was at the princess's residence and knew nothing.

sentences.zh: 智及遣家僮莊桃樹就第殺之，桃樹不忍，執詣智及，久之乃見釋。

translations.literal: Zhi Ji sent household servant Zhuang Taoshu to the residence to kill him; Taoshu could not bear it, seized him and brought him to Zhi Ji, and only after long time was he released.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Ji sent Zhuang Taoshu to kill Shiji; Taoshu could not bear to and brought him to Zhi Ji, who eventually spared him.

sentences.zh: 化及至城門，德戡迎謁，引入朝堂，號為丞相。

translations.literal: When Huaji reached the city gate Dekan met and greeted him, led him into the court hall, and hailed him as Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: At the city gate Dekan welcomed Huaji, led him to court, and hailed him Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 令將帝出江都門以示群賊，因復將入。

translations.literal: He ordered the emperor taken out through the Jiangdu Gate to show the bandit masses, then again brought him in.
translations.idiomatic: He had the emperor shown at Jiangdu Gate to the rebel throng, then brought him back in.

sentences.zh: 遣令狐行達弑帝于宮中。

translations.literal: He sent Linghu Xingda to assassinate the emperor in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Linghu Xingda to assassinate the emperor in the palace.

sentences.zh: 又執朝臣不同己者數十人，及諸王外戚，無少長皆害之。

translations.literal: He again seized several tens of court ministers who did not agree with him, and all the princes and maternal kin without regard to age—all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: He seized dozens of dissenting ministers and all princes and imperial kin without regard to age—and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 唯留秦孝王子浩，立以為帝。

translations.literal: He only kept Qin Xiaowang's son Hao, established him as emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Only Qin Xiaowang's son Hao was spared and set up as emperor.

sentences.zh: 十餘日，奪江都人舟楫，從水路西歸。

translations.literal: After more than ten days they seized the boats of the Jiangdu people and returned west by water route.
translations.idiomatic: After ten days they seized Jiangdu boats and sailed west.

sentences.zh: 至顯福宮，宿公麥孟才、折沖郎將沈光等謀擊化及，反為所害。

translations.literal: Reaching Xianfu Palace, Duke of Public Wheat Meng Cai, Colonel Shen Guang, and others plotted to strike Huaji and were in turn killed by him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianfu Palace Meng Cai and Shen Guang plotted against Huaji and were killed.

sentences.zh: 化及於是入據六宮，其自奉一如煬帝故事。

translations.literal: Huaji thereupon entered and held the six palaces; his own maintenance was just like Emperor Yang's precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji then occupied the six palaces and lived like Emperor Yang.

sentences.zh: 每帳中南面端坐，人有白事者，默然不對。

translations.literal: Each time in the tent he sat facing south at the center; when someone reported affairs he was silent and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: In his tent he sat facing south; when men reported affairs he answered not a word.

sentences.zh: 下牙時，方收取啟狀。

translations.literal: Only when the lower jaw session ended did he gather and take the memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Only after court did he collect the memorials.

sentences.zh: 共奉義、方裕、世良、愷等參決之。

translations.literal: Fengyi, Fangyu, Shiliang, Kai, and others jointly decided them.
translations.idiomatic: Fengyi, Fangyu, Shiliang, Kai, and others decided them jointly.

sentences.zh: 行至徐州，水路不通，復奪人車牛，得二千兩，並載宮人珍寶。

translations.literal: When they reached Xuzhou the water route was blocked; they again seized people's carts and oxen, obtaining two thousand teams, and loaded palace women and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou the waterways were blocked; they seized carts and oxen—two thousand teams—and loaded palace women and treasure.

sentences.zh: 其戈甲戎器，悉令軍士負之。

translations.literal: Their weapons and armor they all ordered the soldiers to carry.
translations.idiomatic: Weapons and armor the soldiers had to carry.

sentences.zh: 道遠疲極，三軍始怨。

translations.literal: The road was long and exhaustion extreme; the three armies at last murmured.
translations.idiomatic: The march wore on; at last the three armies murmured.

sentences.zh: 德戡失望，竊謂行樞曰：「君大誤我。

translations.literal: Dekan was disappointed and secretly said to Xingshu: "You greatly misled me.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan, disappointed, whispered to Xingshu, "You misled me badly.

sentences.zh: 當今撥亂，必藉英賢，化及庸暗，事將必敗，若何？」

translations.literal: To settle chaos today one must rely on heroic worthies; Huaji is mediocre and dim—the affair will surely fail—what then?"
translations.idiomatic: To settle chaos one needs a hero; Huaji is dull—the venture will fail—what then?"

sentences.zh: 行樞曰：「廢之何難！」

translations.literal: Xingshu said: "Deposing him—what difficulty is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Xingshu said, "Deposing him is easy!"

sentences.zh: 因共李孝本、宇文導師、尹正卿等謀，以後軍萬餘兵襲殺化及，立德戡為主。

translations.literal: Thereupon together with Li Xiaoben, Yuwen Daoshi, Yin Zhengqing, and others they plotted, with the rear army of more than ten thousand to surprise and kill Huaji and establish Dekan as leader.
translations.idiomatic: With Li Xiaoben, Yuwen Daoshi, Yin Zhengqing, and others they plotted to kill Huaji with the rear guard of ten thousand and make Dekan leader.

sentences.zh: 弘仁知之，密告化及，盡收德戡及支黨殺之。

translations.literal: Hongren learned of it and secretly told Huaji, who altogether seized Dekan and his faction and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Hongren learned of it and told Huaji, who seized Dekan and his party and killed them.

sentences.zh: 引兵向東郡，通守王軌以城降之。

translations.literal: He led troops toward Dong Commandery; Defender Wang Gui surrendered the city to him.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on Dong Commandery; Wang Gui surrendered the city.

sentences.zh: 元文都推越王侗為主，拜李密為太尉，令擊化及。

translations.literal: Yuan Wendu established Prince Yue Tong as sovereign and appointed Li Mi Grand Marshal, ordering him to strike Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Wendu set up Prince Yue Tong and made Li Mi grand marshal to strike Huaji.

sentences.zh: 密壁清淇，與徐世勣以烽火相應。

translations.literal: Mi walled at Qingqi and with Xu Shiji matched beacon fires.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi fortified Qingqi and matched beacon fires with Xu Shiji.

sentences.zh: 化及數戰不利，其將軍于弘達為密所禽，送於侗所，鑊烹之。

translations.literal: Huaji fought several times without success; his general Yu Hongda was captured by Mi and sent to Tong's place, where he was boiled alive in a cauldron.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji lost battle after battle; Yu Hongda was captured and sent to Tong, where he was boiled alive.

sentences.zh: 化及糧盡，度永濟渠，與密決戰於童山。

translations.literal: Huaji's provisions were exhausted; he crossed the Yongji Canal and with Mi fought the decisive battle at Tong Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Provisions gone, Huaji crossed the Yongji Canal and fought Li Mi at Tong Mountain.

sentences.zh: 遂入汲郡求軍糧，又遣使拷掠東郡人吏，責米粟。

translations.literal: He then entered Ji Commandery seeking army grain, and again sent envoys to torture and plunder the officials and clerks of Dong Commandery, demanding rice and grain.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Ji Commandery for grain and sent men to torture Dong Commandery officials for rice.

sentences.zh: 王軌怨之，以城歸李密。

translations.literal: Wang Gui resented this and returned the city to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui, resentful, surrendered the city to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 化及大懼，自汲郡將圖以北諸州。

translations.literal: Huaji was greatly afraid and from Ji Commandery intended to scheme for the northern commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Huaji planned to flee north from Ji Commandery.

sentences.zh: 其將陳智略率嶺南驍果萬餘人，張童兒率江東驍果數千人，皆叛歸李密。

translations.literal: His generals Chen Zhilue led more than ten thousand valiant guards of Lingnan, Zhang Tong'er led several thousand valiant guards of Jiangdong—all rebelled and returned to Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhilue with ten thousand Lingnan guards and Zhang Tong'er with thousands of Jiangdong guards deserted to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 化及尚有眾二萬，北走魏縣。

translations.literal: Huaji still had twenty thousand men and fled north to Wei County.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji still had twenty thousand men and fled north to Wei County.

sentences.zh: 張愷與其將陳伯謀去之，事覺，為化及所殺。

translations.literal: Zhang Kai with his general Chen Bo plotted to leave him; the affair was discovered and Huaji killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Kai and Chen Bo plotted to desert; discovered, they were killed.

sentences.zh: 腹心稍盡，兵勢日蹙，兄弟更無他計，但相聚酣宴，奏女樂。

translations.literal: His close confidants gradually exhausted, military strength daily pressed; the brothers had no other plan but to gather for deep drinking and play female music.
translations.idiomatic: Confidants dwindled, the army squeezed; the brothers could only drink deep and listen to women's music.

sentences.zh: 醉後，尤智及曰：「我初不知，由汝為計，強來立我。

translations.literal: When drunk he especially blamed Zhi Ji: "At first I did not know; because of your plan you forced me to be established.
translations.idiomatic: Drunk he railed at Zhi Ji, "I never wanted this—you forced the throne on me.

sentences.zh: 今所向無成，負弑主之名，天下所不納。

translations.literal: Now wherever we go there is no success; we bear the name of regicide; the realm will not accept us.
translations.idiomatic: Now we gain nothing and bear the name of regicide—the realm will not have us.

sentences.zh: 滅族豈非由汝乎？」

translations.literal: Extermination of the clan—is it not because of you?"
translations.idiomatic: Our clan's destruction—is it not your fault?"

sentences.zh: 抱其兩子而泣。

translations.literal: He embraced his two sons and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He embraced his two sons and wept.

sentences.zh: 智及怒曰：「事捷之日，都不賜尤；

translations.literal: Zhi Ji angrily said: "When the affair succeeded, you gave me no credit at all;
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Ji raged, "When we won you gave me no credit;

sentences.zh: 及其將敗，乃欲歸罪。

translations.literal: when it is about to fail, you wish to lay blame on me.
translations.idiomatic: now we are failing you blame me.

sentences.zh: 何不殺我以降建德！」

translations.literal: Why not kill me to surrender to Jian De!"
translations.idiomatic: Why not kill me and surrender to Jian De!"

sentences.zh: 兄弟數相鬥鬩，言無長幼，醒而復飲，以此為恆。

translations.literal: The brothers several times mutually fought and quarreled, speaking without respect of age; sobering they again drank—this became their constant.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers quarreled without regard to rank, drank again when sober—this became their habit.

sentences.zh: 自知必敗，乃歎曰：「人生故當死，豈不一日為帝乎！」

translations.literal: Knowing himself sure to fail, he then sighed: "Human life must die in the end—why not be emperor for a single day!"
translations.idiomatic: Knowing defeat was certain, he sighed, "Men must die—why not be emperor for one day!"

sentences.zh: 於是鳩殺浩，僭皇帝位於魏縣，國號許，建元為天壽，置百官。

translations.literal: Thereupon he poisoned Hao, usurped the imperial position at Wei County, state name Xu, era name Heavenly Longevity, and established the hundred offices.
translations.idiomatic: He poisoned Hao, declared himself emperor at Wei County with state name Xu and era Heavenly Longevity, and set up the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 攻元寶藏于魏州，反為所敗，乃東北趣聊城，將招攜海內諸賊。

translations.literal: He attacked Yuan Baocang at Wei Prefecture, was in turn defeated by him, then turned northeast toward Liaocheng intending to rally the bandits of the seas within.
translations.idiomatic: He attacked Yuan Baocang at Wei Prefecture, was beaten, then fled northeast to Liaocheng to rally bandits nationwide.

sentences.zh: 遣士及徇濟北，徵求餉饋。

translations.literal: He sent Shiji to subdue Jibei and levy provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Shiji to scour Jibei for supplies.

sentences.zh: 大唐遣淮安王神通安撫山東，神通圍之十餘日，不克而退。

translations.literal: Great Tang sent Prince of Huai'an Li Shitong to pacify Shandong; Shitong besieged him more than ten days, could not take him, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tang sent Prince Huai'an Li Shitong to pacify Shandong; Shitong besieged him ten days, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 竇建德悉眾攻之。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande with all his forces attacked him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande attacked with his full force.

sentences.zh: 先是，齊州賊帥王薄聞其多寶物，詐來投附。

translations.literal: Earlier, Qizhou bandit chief Wang Bo heard he had many treasures and falsely came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Bo of Qi, hearing of his treasure, feigned submission.

sentences.zh: 化及信之，與共居守。

translations.literal: Huaji trusted him and together with him held guard.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji trusted him and shared the defense.

sentences.zh: 至是，薄引建德入城，禽化及，悉虜其眾。

translations.literal: At this time Bo led Jiande into the city and seized Huaji, capturing all his masses.
translations.idiomatic: Then Bo let Jiande into the city; Huaji was seized and his army captured.

sentences.zh: 先執智及、元武達、孟景、楊士覽、許弘仁等，皆斬之。

translations.literal: First they seized Zhi Ji, Yuan Wuda, Meng Jing, Yang Shiguan, Xu Hongren, and others—all were beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: First they seized Zhi Ji, Yuan Wuda, Meng Jing, Yang Shiguan, Xu Hongren, and others—and beheaded them.

sentences.zh: 及以檻車載化及至大陸縣城下，數其弑逆，並二子承基、承趾皆斬之，傳首於突厥義城公主，梟之虜庭。

translations.literal: When they came, they loaded Huaji in a caged cart to below Dalu County city, counted his regicide, and beheaded both sons Chenggi and Chengzhi; they sent the head to the Tujue Princess of Yicheng and exposed it in the barbarians' court.
translations.idiomatic: They caged Huaji beneath Dalu County, denounced his regicide, and beheaded his sons Chenggi and Chengzhi; the head was sent to Princess Yicheng of the Turks and exposed on the frontier.

sentences.zh: 士及自濟北西歸長安。

translations.literal: Shiji from Jibei returned west to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji returned from Jibei to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 智及幼頑凶，好與人群聚鬥雞，習放鷹狗。

translations.literal: Zhi Ji from youth was stubborn and violent, fond of gathering crowds to cockfight and skilled at flying hawks and dogs.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Ji from youth was violent, loved cockfighting, and trained hawks and hounds.

sentences.zh: 初以父功，賜爵濮陽郡公。

translations.literal: At first through his father's merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Puyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's merit he was enfeoffed Duke of Puyang.

sentences.zh: 蒸淫醜穢，無所不為。

translations.literal: Steaming lust and foul filth—there was nothing he would not do.
translations.idiomatic: His lusts were foul and unrestrained—there was no depravity he shunned.

sentences.zh: 其妻長孫氏，妒而告述。

translations.literal: His wife of the Changsun clan, jealous, reported to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, of the Changsun clan, jealous, reported him to Wenshu.

sentences.zh: 述雖為隱，而大忿之，纖芥之愆，必加鞭棰。

translations.literal: Shu though concealing it was greatly resentful; the slightest fault he was sure to add whipping and flogging.
translations.idiomatic: Wenshu concealed it but was furious; the slightest fault brought the whip.

sentences.zh: 弟士及，恃尚主，又輕忽之。

translations.literal: Younger brother Shiji, relying on marriage to a princess, again treated him lightly.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Shiji, married to a princess, looked down on him.

sentences.zh: 唯化及事事營護，父再三欲殺，輒救免之，由是頗相親昵。

translations.literal: Only Huaji in every matter cared for and protected him; the father several times wished to kill him but always saved and exempted him, and thereby they were rather close and intimate.
translations.idiomatic: Only Huaji protected him; their father several times meant to kill Zhi Ji but Huaji always saved him, and they grew close.

sentences.zh: 遂勸化及遣人入蕃，私為交易。

translations.literal: Thereupon he urged Huaji to send men into the frontier tribes to trade privately.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Huaji to send men beyond the frontier for private trade.

sentences.zh: 事發，當誅，述獨證智及罪惡，而為化及請命，帝因兩釋之。

translations.literal: When the affair broke out they should have been executed; Shu alone testified to Zhi Ji's crimes and evil and yet pleaded for Huaji's life—the emperor therefore released both.
translations.idiomatic: When it was discovered they should have died; Wenshu alone testified to Zhi Ji's crimes yet pleaded for Huaji, and the emperor spared both.

sentences.zh: 述將死，抗表言其凶勃，必且破家。

translations.literal: When Shu was about to die he submitted a defiant memorial saying Zhi Ji was fierce and overbearing and would surely destroy the family.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenshu was dying he warned that Zhi Ji was violent and would destroy the clan.

sentences.zh: 帝后思述，拜智及將作少監。

translations.literal: The emperor and empress later missed Shu and appointed Zhi Ji Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor missed Wenshu and made Zhi Ji director of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 其江都弑逆事，皆智及之謀也。

translations.literal: The Jiangdu regicide affair was all Zhi Ji's plotting.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangdu regicide was Zhi Ji's plot.

sentences.zh: 化及為丞相，以為右僕射，領十二衛大將軍。

translations.literal: When Huaji was chancellor he made him Right Vice Minister and commander of the twelve guards.
translations.idiomatic: As chancellor Huaji made him right vice minister and commander of the twelve guards.

sentences.zh: 及僭號，封齊王。

translations.literal: When he usurped the throne he enfeoffed him Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji usurped the throne he enfeoffed him Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 竇建德獲而斬之，並其党十餘人，皆暴死梟首。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande captured and beheaded him, and his faction of more than ten men—all died exposed with heads hung.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande captured and beheaded him and more than ten of his party—all exposed headless.

sentences.zh: 司馬德戡，扶風雍人。

translations.literal: Sima Dekan was a man of Yong in Fufeng.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Dekan was from Yong in Fufeng.

sentences.zh: 父元謙，仕周為都督。

translations.literal: His father Yuanqian served Zhou as commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanqian served Zhou as a commander.

sentences.zh: 德戡幼孤，以屠豕自給。

translations.literal: Dekan was orphaned young and supported himself by butchering pigs.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, Dekan made his living butchering pigs.

sentences.zh: 有桑門釋粲，通德戡母娥氏，遂撫教之，因解書計。

translations.literal: There was a monk Shi Can who knew Dekan's mother Lady E; he then fostered and taught him, and thereby he understood writing and reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: Monk Shi Can knew his mother Lady E, raised and taught him, and he learned letters and reckoning.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為侍官，漸遷至大都督。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang he was a palace attendant and was promoted in succession to Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaihuang he was a palace attendant and rose to grand commander.

sentences.zh: 從楊素出討漢王諒，充內營左右。

translations.literal: Following Yang Su on campaign against Prince Han Liang, he filled the inner camp's left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Following Yang Su against Prince Han Liang, he served in the inner camp.

sentences.zh: 進止便僻，俊辯多奸計，素大善之。

translations.literal: In advancing and halting he was nimble and obsequious, handsome in debate with many treacherous schemes—Su greatly favored him.
translations.idiomatic: Nimble in camp, eloquent and treacherous—Su favored him greatly.

sentences.zh: 以勳授儀同三司。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted Protocol Equal to Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: For merit he received protocol equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，為鷹揚郎將。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye he was Hawkish Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye year three he was hawkish guard general.

sentences.zh: 從討遼左，進位正議大夫，遷武賁郎將。

translations.literal: Following the campaign in eastern Liao, he was promoted to Correct Counselor and transferred to Martial Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign he rose to correct counselor and martial guard general.

sentences.zh: 煬帝甚昵之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yang was very intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang favored him warmly.

sentences.zh: 從至江都，領左右備身驍果萬人，營於城內。

translations.literal: Following to Jiangdu, he commanded the left and right personal guard valiant forces of ten thousand men, encamped within the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangdu he commanded ten thousand personal guard valiant troops encamped in the city.

sentences.zh: 因隋末大亂，乃率驍果反，語在化及事中。

translations.literal: Because at the end of Sui there was great chaos, he then led the valiant guards in rebellion—the words are in the Huaji affair.
translations.idiomatic: As Sui collapsed he led the valiant guards in rebellion—as told in the Huaji account.

sentences.zh: 既獲煬帝，與党孟景等推化及為丞相。

translations.literal: After they obtained the emperor, with the faction Meng Jing and others they pushed Huaji as chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: After seizing the emperor he and Meng Jing's faction made Huaji chancellor.

sentences.zh: 化及首封德戡為溫國公，加光祿大夫，仍統本兵。

translations.literal: Huaji first enfeoffed Dekan Duke of the State of Wen, added Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, and still commanded the original troops.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji first enfeoffed him Duke of Wen, made him grand master for splendid happiness, and left him his troops.

sentences.zh: 化及意甚忌之。

translations.literal: Huaji's intent greatly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 後數日，化及署諸將，分配士卒，乃以德戡為禮部尚書，外示美遷，實奪其兵也。

translations.literal: Several days later Huaji assigned the various generals and distributed soldiers and troops, then made Dekan Minister of Rites—outwardly showing a fine transfer, in reality seizing his army.
translations.idiomatic: Days later Huaji reassigned commanders, made Dekan minister of rites—a fine title that stripped him of troops.

sentences.zh: 由是懷怨，所獲賞物皆賂于智及，智及為之言。

translations.literal: Thereby he harbored resentment; whatever rewards he obtained he all bribed to Zhi Ji, and Zhi Ji spoke for him.
translations.idiomatic: Resentful, he bribed Zhi Ji with his rewards, and Zhi Ji spoke for him.

sentences.zh: 行至徐州，舍舟登陸，令德戡將後軍。

translations.literal: When they reached Xuzhou they left boats and went ashore, ordering Dekan to command the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: At Xuzhou they left the boats and put Dekan in charge of the rear.

sentences.zh: 乃與趙行樞、李孝本、尹正卿、宇文導師等謀襲化及，遣人使于孟海公，結為外助。

translations.literal: Thereupon with Zhao Xingshu, Li Xiaoben, Yin Zhengqing, Yuwen Daoshi, and others they plotted to surprise Huaji, sending men to Meng Haigong to join as external aid.
translations.idiomatic: With Zhao Xingshu, Li Xiaoben, Yin Zhengqing, Yuwen Daoshi, and others he plotted to strike Huaji and sent to Meng Haigong for aid.

sentences.zh: 遷延未發，以待使報。

translations.literal: They delayed and did not rise, waiting for the envoy's report.
