translations.idiomatic: They delayed, awaiting the envoy's reply.

sentences.zh: 許弘仁、張愷知之，以告化及。

translations.literal: Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai learned of it and told Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hongren and Zhang Kai learned of it and told Huaji.

sentences.zh: 因遣其弟士及陽為遊獵，至於後軍。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his younger brother Shiji under pretense of hunting to go to the rear army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his brother Shiji under pretense of hunting to the rear army.

sentences.zh: 德戡不知事露，出營參謁，因命執之，並其黨與。

translations.literal: Dekan did not know the affair was exposed, came out of camp to pay respects, and was thereupon ordered seized together with his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan, not knowing it was exposed, came out to pay respects and was seized with his party.

sentences.zh: 化及責之曰：「與公戮力共定海內，出於萬死。

translations.literal: Huaji reproached him saying: "With you, sir, we strove together to settle the seas within, emerging from ten thousand deaths.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji reproached him, "We strove through ten thousand deaths to settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 今始事成，願得同守富貴，公又何為反也？」

translations.literal: Now the affair has just succeeded and I wish to guard riches together with you—why, sir, do you again rebel?"
translations.idiomatic: Now we have just won and I wished to share fortune—why rebel again?"

sentences.zh: 德戡曰：「本殺昏主，苦其毒害。

translations.literal: Dekan said: "Originally we killed the dim sovereign, bitter at his poisonous harm.
translations.idiomatic: Dekan said, "We killed the tyrant because of his poison.

sentences.zh: 立足下而又甚之，逼於物情，不獲已也。」

translations.literal: I stand beneath you and you are still more so, pressed by the feelings of things—I could not avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: Now you are worse—driven by circumstance I had no choice."

sentences.zh: 化及不對，命送至幕下，縊而殺之。

translations.literal: Huaji did not reply and ordered him sent below the tent and strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji made no answer and had him strangled below the tent.

sentences.zh: 裴虔通，河東人。

translations.literal: Pei Qiantong was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qiantong was from Hedong.

sentences.zh: 初，煬帝為晉王，以親信從，稍遷至監門校尉。

translations.literal: At first, when Emperor Yang was Prince of Jin, Qiantong followed him as a trusted intimate, and gradually rose to Commandant of the Gate Guards.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang was still Prince of Jin, Qiantong followed him as a trusted man and gradually rose to Commandant of the Gate Guards.

sentences.zh: 帝即位，擢舊左右，授宣惠尉。

translations.literal: When the emperor ascended the throne, he promoted his old attendants and appointed Qiantong Xuanhui Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor took the throne, he promoted his old attendants and appointed Qiantong Xuanhui Commandant.

sentences.zh: 累從征役，至通議大夫。

translations.literal: He repeatedly followed on campaigns and service, reaching Grand Master for Comprehensive Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly accompanied campaigns and expeditions, rising to Grand Master for Comprehensive Counsel.

sentences.zh: 與司馬德戡同謀作亂，先開宮門，騎至成象殿，殺將軍獨孤盛，執帝於西閤。

translations.literal: He plotted rebellion together with Sima Dekan, first opened the palace gates, rode to Chengxiang Hall, killed General Dugu Sheng, and seized the emperor at the western chamber.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Sima Dekan’s plot, opened the palace gates first, rode to Chengxiang Hall, killed General Dugu Sheng, and seized the emperor in the western chamber.

sentences.zh: 化及以虔通為光祿大夫、莒國公。

translations.literal: Huaji made Qiantong Grandee of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji appointed Qiantong Grandee of Splendid Happiness and Duke of Ju.

sentences.zh: 化及引兵之北也，令鎮徐州。

translations.literal: When Huaji led the troops north, he ordered him to garrison Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji led the army north, he ordered Qiantong to garrison Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 化及敗後，歸於大唐，即授徐州總管，轉辰州刺史，封長蛇男。

translations.literal: After Huaji was defeated, Qiantong submitted to the Great Tang and was at once appointed Area Commander of Xuzhou, transferred to Inspector of Chenzhou, and enfeoffed as Baron of Changshe.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji’s defeat, Qiantong submitted to the Great Tang. He was immediately appointed Area Commander of Xuzhou, then transferred as Inspector of Chenzhou and enfeoffed Baron of Changshe.

sentences.zh: 尋以隋朝弑逆之罪，除名，徙於嶺表而死。

translations.literal: Soon, for the crime of regicide and rebellion against the Sui court, his name was removed from the rolls, and he was exiled beyond the passes, where he died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, for the crime of regicide and rebellion under the Sui, he was struck from the rolls and exiled beyond the Lingnan passes, where he died.

sentences.zh: 王世充，字行滿，本西域胡人也。

translations.literal: Wang Shichong, style name Xingman, was originally a Hu man of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shichong, courtesy name Xingman, was originally a Hu from the Western Regions.

sentences.zh: 祖支頹褥，徙居新豐。

translations.literal: His grandfather Zhi Tuilu moved to reside at Xinfeng.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Zhi Tuilu moved to Xinfeng.

sentences.zh: 頹褥死，其妻少寡，與儀同王粲野合，生子曰瓊，粲遂納之以為小妻。

translations.literal: Tuilu died; his wife was young and a widow and had illicit union with Palace Companion Wang Can in the wild; she bore a son named Qiong, and Can then took her in as a minor wife.
translations.idiomatic: Tuilu died; his young widow lay with palace companion Wang Can and bore a son Qiong; Can took her as concubine.

sentences.zh: 其父收幼孤，隨母嫁粲，粲愛而養焉，因姓王氏。

translations.literal: His father received the young orphan and followed the mother in marrying Can; Can loved and raised him, and thereby took the surname Wang.
translations.idiomatic: His father was raised by Can after the marriage and took the surname Wang.

sentences.zh: 官至懷、汴二州長史。

translations.literal: His office reached long administrator of Huai and Bian prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to long administrator of Huai and Bian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 世充捲髮豺聲，沉猜多詭詐，頗窺書傳，尤好兵法，曉龜策推步盈虛，然未嘗為人言也。

translations.literal: Shichong had curly hair and a jackal's voice, deep suspicion and much treacherous scheming; he somewhat peered into books and records, especially loved military methods, understood tortoise divination and calculating surplus and shortage, yet never spoke of it to people.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had curly hair and a harsh voice, was deep and treacherous, read widely especially in military arts and divination, yet never spoke of it.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，為左翊衛，後以軍功拜儀同，授兵部員外郎。

translations.literal: In Kaihuang he was Left Wing Guard; later through military merit he was appointed Palace Companion and given the post of Aide in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Under Kaihuang he was left wing guard; later by military merit he became palace companion and war ministry aide.

sentences.zh: 善敷奏，明習法律，而舞弄文墨，高下在心。

translations.literal: He was skilled at memorials and clear in laws, yet manipulated documents and ink, high and low in his heart.
translations.idiomatic: He excelled at memorials and knew law, yet twisted documents to his will.

sentences.zh: 或有駁難之者，世充利口飾非，辭義鋒起，從雖知其否而莫能屈，稱為明辯。

translations.literal: If someone rebutted him, Shichong with sharp mouth adorned wrongs and meanings clashed—followers though knowing it was false could not bend him, and called him clear in debate.
translations.idiomatic: When challenged he talked his way out with a sharp tongue; men knew he was wrong yet could not refute him and called him eloquent.

sentences.zh: 煬帝世，累遷至江都郡丞。

translations.literal: In Emperor Yang's time he was promoted in succession to Jiangdu Commandery aide.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang he rose to Jiangdu commandery aide.

sentences.zh: 時帝數幸江都，世充善候人主顏色，阿諛順旨，每入言事，帝善之。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor several times visited Jiangdu; Shichong was skilled at watching the sovereign's countenance, flattering and following intent; each time he entered to speak on affairs the emperor was pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor often visited Jiangdu; Shichong watched his mood, flattered him, and pleased him whenever he spoke.

sentences.zh: 又以郡丞領江都宮監，乃雕飾池台，陰奏遠方珍物，以媚於帝，由是益昵之。

translations.literal: Again as commandery aide he led the Jiangdu Palace Directorate; he carved and adorned pools and terraces, secretly memorialized distant rare objects to charm the emperor, and thereby was still more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: As commandery aide he oversaw the Jiangdu palace, adorned pools and terraces, and sent rare tribute to win favor.

sentences.zh: 大業八年，隋始亂，世充內懷徼幸，卑身禮士，陰結豪俊，多收眾心。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Daye Sui first fell into chaos; Shichong inwardly harbored lucky chance, humbled himself and honored scholars, secretly joined heroic worthies, and widely gathered people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: In Daye eight, as Sui collapsed, Shichong courted fortune, humbled himself before scholars, and secretly won heroes' hearts.

sentences.zh: 江淮間人素輕薄，又屬賊盜群起，人多犯法，有系獄抵罪者，世充枉法出之，以樹私恩。

translations.literal: Men between the Yangtze and Huai were by nature always frivolous; again bandits and robbers rose in groups and many men violated law—those bound in prison facing punishment Shichong perverted law to release, to plant private favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang-Huai men were frivolous; as bandits rose he illegally freed prisoners to buy loyalty.

sentences.zh: 及楊玄感反，吳人硃燮、晉陵人管崇起兵江南以應之，自稱將軍，擁眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Wu man Zhu Xie and Jinjing man Guan Chong raised troops in Jiangnan to respond, calling themselves generals and gathering masses of more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, Zhu Xie of Wu and Guan Chong of Jinjing raised Jiangnan with over a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 帝遣將軍吐萬緒、魚俱羅討之，不能克。

translations.literal: The emperor sent Generals Tu Wanxu and Yu Juluo to attack them and could not overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Tu Wanxu and Yu Juluo; they could not win.

sentences.zh: 世充募江都萬餘人，擊頻破之。

translations.literal: Shichong recruited more than ten thousand men of Jiangdu and struck, frequently defeating them.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong raised ten thousand Jiangdu men and repeatedly defeated them.

sentences.zh: 每有克捷，必歸功於下，所獲軍實，皆推與士卒，身無所取。

translations.literal: Each time there was victory he was sure to attribute merit to subordinates; military goods obtained he all pushed to the soldiers—nothing for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He always credited subordinates and gave all booty to the troops, keeping nothing.

sentences.zh: 由此人爭為用，功最居多。

translations.literal: Thereby men vied to be used by him; his achievements were the most numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Men vied to serve him; his victories were the greatest.

sentences.zh: 十年，齊郡賊帥孟讓自長白山寇掠諸郡，至盱眙，有眾十餘萬。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Qi Commandery bandit chief Meng Rang from Changbai Mountain raided and plundered the commanderies, reaching Xuyi with masses of more than a hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten Meng Rang of Qi from Changbai raided the commanderies to Xuyi with a hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 世充以兵拒之，而羸師示弱，保都梁山為五柵，相持不戰。

translations.literal: Shichong with troops resisted him but with a weakened army showed weakness, holding Mount Liangshan in the capital with five palisades, facing off without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong resisted but feigned weakness, holding Mount Liangshan in five camps without fighting.

sentences.zh: 後因其懈馳，出兵奮擊，大破之，乘勝盡滅諸賊，讓以數十騎遁去，斬首萬人，六畜軍資，莫不盡獲。

translations.literal: Later taking advantage of their slackness he galloped out troops in fierce attack, greatly defeated them, pressed the victory and extinguished all the bandits; Rang with several tens of horsemen fled away; beheaded heads ten thousand, livestock and army goods—all were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: When they slackened he struck, routed them, destroyed the bandits; Rang fled with dozens of horsemen; ten thousand heads fell and all booty was taken.

sentences.zh: 帝以世充有將帥才略，始遣領兵，討諸小盜，所向破之。

translations.literal: The emperor because Shichong had general's talent and strategy first sent him to lead troops to attack the lesser bandits; wherever he went he broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing his talent, the emperor sent him against lesser bandits and he broke them wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 然性多矯偽，詐為善，能自勤苦，以求聲譽。

translations.literal: Yet his nature was much pretense and fraud, feigning goodness, able to toil bitterly himself to seek reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was pretentious, feigned virtue, and toiled publicly for reputation.

sentences.zh: 十一年，突厥圍帝於雁門，世充盡發江都人往赴難。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the Turks besieged the emperor at Yanmen; Shichong mustered all Jiangdu men to go to the rescue.
translations.idiomatic: In year eleven, when Turks besieged Yanmen, he mustered all Jiangdu to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 在軍中，垢面悲泣，曉夜不解甲，藉草而坐。

translations.literal: In the army his face was filthy and he wept in grief, day and night not removing armor, sitting on straw.
translations.idiomatic: In camp he wept with a filthy face, never removing armor, sitting on straw.

sentences.zh: 帝聞之，以為愛己，益信任之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of it and thought he loved him, trusting him still more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought this showed devotion and trusted him more.

sentences.zh: 十二年，遷為江都通守。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was transferred to Jiangdu transit governor.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve he became Jiangdu transit governor.

sentences.zh: 時厭次人格謙為盜數年，兵十餘萬，在豆子<鹵亢>中。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Qian of Yanci had been a bandit for several years with troops of more than a hundred thousand in the Douzi marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Qian of Yanci had been a bandit for years with a hundred thousand men in the Douzi marshes.

sentences.zh: 世充破斬之，威振群賊。

translations.literal: Shichong defeated and beheaded him, his might shaking the bandit hosts.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong defeated and killed him, shaking the bandits.

sentences.zh: 又擊盧明月，破之於南陽。

translations.literal: Again he struck Lu Mingyue and defeated him at Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Lu Mingyue at Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 後還江都，帝大悅，自執杯酒以賜之。

translations.literal: Later returning to Jiangdu the emperor was greatly pleased and himself held a cup of wine to bestow on him.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to Jiangdu the emperor himself gave him a cup of wine.

sentences.zh: 時世充又知帝好內，乃言江淮良家多有美女，願備後庭，無由自進。

translations.literal: At that time Shichong again knew the emperor loved the inner palace and therefore said that good families of the Jiang-Huai had many beautiful women and he wished to prepare the rear court but had no way to advance himself.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor loved women, he said Jiang-Huai had many beauties for the rear court but he could not present them himself.

sentences.zh: 帝愈喜，因密令世充閱觀諸女，資質端麗合法相者，取正庫及應入京物以聘納之。

translations.literal: The emperor was still more pleased and therefore secretly ordered Shichong to review all the women; those of fine quality and appearance fitting the physiognomy he took from the main treasury and goods that should enter the capital to betroth and receive them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor secretly ordered him to select women of fine looks and betroth them with treasury goods.

sentences.zh: 所用不可勝計，帳上所司雲敕別用，不顯其實。

translations.literal: What was used could not be counted; the office above the accounts said imperial orders separately provided, not showing the reality.
translations.idiomatic: The cost was beyond counting; accounts were hidden under separate imperial orders.

sentences.zh: 有合意者，則厚賞世充，或不中者，又以賚之。

translations.literal: If there were those who pleased him he then richly rewarded Shichong; if some did not please, again he bestowed them on him.
translations.idiomatic: If the emperor was pleased he richly rewarded Shichong; if not, he still gave him gifts.

sentences.zh: 後令以船送東京，而道路賊起，使者苦役，于淮泗中沉船溺殺之者，前後十數。

translations.literal: Later he ordered them sent by boat to the Eastern Capital, but bandits rose on the roads; envoys suffered the labor, and in the Huai and Si rivers those who sank boats and drowned the killed—before and after there were more than ten.
translations.idiomatic: They were to be sent by boat to the Eastern Capital; bandits blocked the roads; envoys drowned women in the Huai and Si—more than ten such cases.

sentences.zh: 或有髮露，世充為秘之，又遽簡閱以供進。

translations.literal: Some were exposed; Shichong concealed it and again hurriedly reviewed and supplied for presentation.
translations.idiomatic: When exposed Shichong concealed it and hurried more women forward.

sentences.zh: 是後益見親昵。

translations.literal: After this he was still more seen as intimate.
translations.idiomatic: After this he grew still more intimate.

sentences.zh: 遇李密攻陷興洛倉，進逼東都，官軍數敗，光祿大夫裴仁基以武牢降於密。

translations.literal: It happened that Li Mi attacked and took Xingluo Granary, pressed the Eastern Capital, and the government troops several times were defeated; Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Pei Renji with Wulao surrendered to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi took Xingluo Granary and pressed the Eastern Capital; government troops were repeatedly beaten; Pei Renji surrendered Wulao to Mi.

sentences.zh: 帝惡之，大發兵，將討焉。

translations.literal: The emperor hated this and greatly sent troops, intending to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, angered, mobilized a great army to strike him.

sentences.zh: 特發中詔遣世充為將，軍於洛口以拒密。

translations.literal: He specially issued a secret edict dispatching Shichong as general, encamping at Luokou to resist Mi.
translations.idiomatic: A secret edict sent Shichong as general to camp at Luokou and hold Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 前後百餘戰，互有勝負。

translations.literal: Before and after there were more than a hundred battles, each side having victory and defeat.
translations.idiomatic: They fought more than a hundred battles, each side winning some.

sentences.zh: 世充乃引軍度洛水，逼倉城。

translations.literal: Shichong then led the army across the Luo River and pressed Granary City.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong crossed the Luo and pressed the granary city.

sentences.zh: 李密與戰。

translations.literal: Li Mi fought with him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi gave battle.

sentences.zh: 世充敗績，赴水溺死者萬餘人。

translations.literal: Shichong was defeated; those who rushed into the water and drowned numbered more than ten thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong was routed; more than ten thousand drowned in the river.

sentences.zh: 時天寒，大雨雪，兵既度水，衣皆沾濕，在道凍死者又數萬人，比至河陽，才以千數。

translations.literal: At that time the weather was cold with great rain and snow; the troops having crossed the water, their clothes were all soaked, and on the road those who froze to death were again several tens of thousands—when they reached Heyang only about a thousand remained.
translations.idiomatic: It was bitter cold with rain and snow; clothes froze on their backs and tens of thousands died on the march—only a thousand reached Heyang.

sentences.zh: 世充自系獄請罪，越王侗遣使赦之，召令還都。

translations.literal: Shichong himself bound himself in prison to request punishment; Prince Yue Tong sent envoys to pardon him and summoned him to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong bound himself and asked punishment; Prince Yue Tong pardoned him and recalled him to the capital.

sentences.zh: 收合亡散，屯於含嘉城中，不敢復出。

translations.literal: He gathered and united the scattered and lost, encamped in Hancheng, and dared not come out again.
translations.idiomatic: He gathered the survivors, held Hancheng, and dared not venture out.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及殺帝于江都，世充與太府卿元文都、將軍皇甫無逸、右司郎盧楚奉侗為主。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji killed the emperor at Jiangdu; Shichong with Grand Treasury Director Yuan Wendu, General Huangfu Wuyi, and Right Department Aide Lu Chu supported Tong as sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: When Huaji killed the emperor at Jiangdu, Shichong with Yuan Wendu, Huangfu Wuyi, and Lu Chu set up Prince Yue Tong.

sentences.zh: 侗以世充為吏部尚書，封鄭國公。

translations.literal: Tong made Shichong Minister of Personnel and enfeoffed him Duke of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: Tong made Shichong minister of personnel and enfeoffed him Duke of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 及侗用元文都、盧楚之謀，拜李密為太尉、尚書令，密遂稱臣，復以兵拒化及于黎陽，遣使獻捷。

translations.literal: When Tong used Yuan Wendu and Lu Chu's plan to appoint Li Mi Grand Marshal and Director of the Masters, Mi thereupon declared himself minister and again with troops resisted Huaji at Liyang, sending envoys to present victory reports.
translations.idiomatic: Tong followed Wendu and Lu Chu's plan to make Li Mi grand marshal; Mi submitted, fought Huaji at Liyang, and sent victory reports.

sentences.zh: 眾皆悅，世充獨謂其麾下諸將曰：「文都之輩，刀筆吏耳。

translations.literal: The masses were all pleased; Shichong alone said to his generals below: "Wendu's crowd are mere pen clerks.
translations.idiomatic: All rejoiced; Shichong alone told his generals, "Wendu's crowd are mere clerks.

sentences.zh: 吾觀其勢，必為李密所禽。

translations.literal: I observe their situation—they will surely be captured by Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: I see they will fall to Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 且吾軍人馬每與密戰，殺其父兄子弟，前後已多，一旦為之下，吾屬無類矣。」

translations.literal: Moreover our soldiers and horses have fought Mi each time, killing his fathers, brothers, sons, and nephews—already many before and after; once we are beneath him, our sort will be wiped out."
translations.idiomatic: Our men have killed Mi's kin in battle after battle; if we bow to him we are finished."

sentences.zh: 出此言以激怒其眾。

translations.literal: He spoke these words to anger his masses.
translations.idiomatic: He said this to inflame his troops.

sentences.zh: 文都知而大懼，與楚等謀，將因世充入內，伏甲而殺之。

translations.literal: Wendu learned of it and was greatly afraid; with Chu and others he plotted, intending when Shichong entered the palace to set ambush and kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu, terrified, plotted with Chu to ambush Shichong in the palace.

sentences.zh: 期有日矣，將軍段達遣女婿張志以楚等謀告之。

translations.literal: The day was fixed; General Duan Da sent his son-in-law Zhang Zhi to report Chu and the others' plot to him.
translations.idiomatic: The day was set; Duan Da's son-in-law Zhang Zhi revealed the plot.

sentences.zh: 世充夜勒兵圍宮城，將軍費曜、田世闍等與戰於東太陽門外。

translations.literal: Shichong by night restrained troops and surrounded the palace city; Generals Fei Yao, Tian Shikan, and others fought with him outside the East Sun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong by night surrounded the palace; Fei Yao and Tian Shikan fought him at the East Sun Gate.

sentences.zh: 曜軍敗，世充遂攻門而入。

translations.literal: Yao's army was defeated and Shichong attacked the gate and entered.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was beaten and Shichong broke in.

sentences.zh: 無逸以單騎遁走。

translations.literal: Wuyi with a single horse fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Wuyi fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 獲楚，殺之。

translations.literal: They seized Chu and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: They seized Chu and killed him.

sentences.zh: 時宮門尚閉，世充遣人扣門言於侗曰：「元文都等欲執皇帝降于李密，段達知而以告臣。

translations.literal: At that time the palace gates were still closed; Shichong sent men to knock on the gate and speak to Tong: "Yuan Wendu and the others wish to seize the emperor and surrender to Li Mi; Duan Da knew and told me.
translations.idiomatic: The gates were still shut; Shichong sent word to Tong, "Wendu meant to hand you to Li Mi; Duan Da warned me.

sentences.zh: 臣非敢反，誅反者耳。」

translations.literal: Your servant dares not rebel—I am killing rebels, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I do not rebel—I kill rebels, that is all."

sentences.zh: 文都聞變，入奉侗于乾陽殿，陳兵衛之。

translations.literal: Wendu heard of the change, entered to attend Tong in the Qianyang Hall, and arrayed troops to guard him.
translations.idiomatic: Wendu heard and brought Tong to Qianyang Hall under guard.

sentences.zh: 令將帥乘城以拒難，兵敗，侗命開門以納世充。

translations.literal: He ordered the generals to mount the walls to resist the calamity; the troops were defeated and Tong ordered the gates opened to admit Shichong.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the walls held; when troops failed Tong opened the gates to Shichong.

sentences.zh: 世充悉遣人代宿衛者，明日入謁，頓首流涕而言曰：「文都等無狀，謀相屠害，事急為此，不敢背國。」

translations.literal: Shichong altogether sent men to replace the night guards; the next day he entered audience, prostrated himself weeping and said: "Wendu and the others were without propriety, plotting mutual slaughter; the affair was urgent so I did this—I dare not betray the state."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong replaced the guards; next day he knelt weeping, "Wendu plotted murder in urgency—I could not betray the state."

sentences.zh: 侗與之盟。

translations.literal: Tong made a covenant with him.
translations.idiomatic: Tong made peace with him.

sentences.zh: 世充尋遣韋節等諷侗，命拜為尚書左僕射、總督內外諸軍事。

translations.literal: Shichong soon sent Wei Jie and others to hint to Tong, ordering him appointed Left Vice Minister of the Masters and commander of all internal and external military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had Wei Jie urge Tong to make him left vice minister and supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 又授其兄惲為內史令，入居禁中。

translations.literal: He again appointed his elder brother Yun Interior Secretary and dwelling within the forbidden precinct.
translations.idiomatic: He made his brother Yun interior secretary and moved into the palace.

sentences.zh: 未幾，李密破化及還，其勁兵良馬多戰死，士卒皆倦。

translations.literal: Before long Li Mi defeated Huaji and returned; his crack troops and fine horses mostly died in battle and the soldiers were all weary.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Mi defeated Huaji and returned, his best troops dead and his men exhausted.

sentences.zh: 世充欲乘其弊而擊之，恐人心不一，乃假託鬼神，言夢見周公，乃立祠于洛水之上，遣巫宣言周公欲令僕射急討李密，當有大功，不則兵皆疫死。

translations.literal: Shichong wished to take advantage of their weakness and strike them but feared hearts were not one; he therefore falsely used spirits and demons, saying he dreamed of the Duke of Zhou, then established a shrine on the Luo River, sent shamans proclaiming the Duke of Zhou wished the Vice Minister urgently to attack Li Mi and there would be great merit—otherwise the troops would all die of plague.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong wished to strike but feared disunity; he feigned a dream of the Duke of Zhou, built a shrine on the Luo, and had shamans say the duke demanded an attack on Li Mi or the army would perish of plague.

sentences.zh: 世充兵多楚人，俗信妖妄，故出此言以惑之。

translations.literal: Shichong's troops were mostly Chu men; custom believed in demonic delusion, so he spoke thus to delude them.
translations.idiomatic: His troops were mostly Chu men who believed in omens—so he deceived them.

sentences.zh: 眾皆請戰，世充簡練精勇得二萬餘人，馬千餘匹，營洛水南。

translations.literal: The masses all requested battle; Shichong selected and trained elite brave men obtaining more than twenty thousand, horses more than a thousand, and encamped south of the Luo.
translations.idiomatic: All clamored for battle; he picked twenty thousand elite and a thousand horses and camped south of the Luo.

sentences.zh: 密軍偃師北山上，時密新得志於化及，有輕世充之心，不設壁壘。

translations.literal: Mi's army was on the northern mountain at Yanshi; at that time Mi had just gained his will against Huaji and held Shichong lightly, not setting ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi camped on the northern hills at Yanshi, fresh from victory over Huaji, despising Shichong and building no ramparts.

sentences.zh: 世充遣二百餘騎，潛入北山，伏溪穀中，令軍秣馬蓐食。

translations.literal: Shichong sent more than two hundred horsemen secretly into the northern mountain, hiding in streams and valleys, ordering the army to feed horses and sleep in the open.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent two hundred horsemen to hide in the northern hills and valleys and ordered the army to feed horses and sleep rough.

sentences.zh: 既而宵濟，人馬賓士，比明而薄密。

translations.literal: Thereupon at night they crossed; men and horses were numerous guests—by dawn they pressed Mi.
translations.idiomatic: At night they crossed; by dawn they were upon Li Mi.

sentences.zh: 密出兵應之，陣未成列而兩軍合戰，其伏兵蔽山而上，潛登北原，乘高而下，壓密營。

translations.literal: Mi sent troops to respond; the battle lines were not yet formed in ranks when the two armies joined battle; the ambush troops covered the mountain and ascended, secretly climbing the northern plateau, riding the height and descending, pressing Mi's camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi met them before his lines were formed; the ambush climbed the heights and fell on the camp.

sentences.zh: 營中亂，無能拒者，即入縱火。

translations.literal: In the camp there was chaos and none could resist; they at once entered and set fires.
translations.idiomatic: The camp collapsed; they entered and set fires.

sentences.zh: 密軍大驚而潰，降其將張童兒、陳智略。

translations.literal: Mi's army was greatly alarmed and routed; they surrendered his generals Zhang Tong'er and Chen Zhilue.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi's army broke; Zhang Tong'er and Chen Zhilue surrendered.

sentences.zh: 進下偃師。

translations.literal: They advanced and took Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: They took Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 初，世充兄偉及子玄應隋化及至東郡，密得而囚之於城中。

translations.literal: At first Shichong's elder brother Wei and son Xuanying followed Sui to Huaji at Dong Commandery; Mi obtained and imprisoned them in the city.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's brother Wei and son Xuanying had been taken prisoner in the city.

sentences.zh: 至是，盡獲之。

translations.literal: At this time they were all obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Now they were recovered.

sentences.zh: 又執密長史邴元真妻子、司馬鄭虔象之母及諸將子弟，皆撫慰之，各令潛呼其父兄。

translations.literal: Again they seized Mi's chief clerk Bing Yuanzhen's wife and children, Secretary Zheng Qianxiang's mother, and the sons and younger brothers of the various generals—all were comforted, each ordered secretly to call their fathers and elder brothers.
translations.idiomatic: They seized the families of Bing Yuanzhen, Zheng Qianxiang, and other officers, comforted them, and had them call their kin.

sentences.zh: 兵次洛口，元真、鄭虔象等舉倉城以應之。

translations.literal: When the army halted at Luokou, Yuanzhen, Zheng Qianxiang, and others raised Granary City in response.
translations.idiomatic: At Luokou Yuanzhen and Zheng Qianxiang opened the granary city to him.

sentences.zh: 密以數十騎遁逸，世充收其眾而還。

translations.literal: Mi with several tens of horsemen fled in escape; Shichong gathered his masses and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi fled with a few dozen horsemen; Shichong gathered the army and returned.

sentences.zh: 東盡于海，南至於江，悉來歸附。

translations.literal: East to the sea, south to the river—all came to submit and attach.
translations.idiomatic: From the sea to the south all submitted.

sentences.zh: 世充又令韋節諷侗，拜己為太尉，置署官屬，以尚書省為其府。

translations.literal: Shichong again ordered Wei Jie to hint to Tong, appointing himself Grand Marshal, establishing office staff, taking the Masters Ministry as his headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong had Wei Jie urge Tong to make him grand marshal and take the Masters Ministry as his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋自稱鄭王，遣其將高略帥師攻壽安，不利而旋。

translations.literal: Soon he himself called himself King of Zheng and sent his general Gao Lue to lead troops attacking Shou'an, unfavorable and returning.
translations.idiomatic: He declared himself King of Zheng and sent Gao Lue against Shou'an without success.

sentences.zh: 又帥師攻圍穀州，三日而退。

translations.literal: Again he led troops attacking and besieging Gu Prefecture, three days then withdrawing.
translations.idiomatic: He besieged Gu Prefecture three days and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 明年，自稱相國，受九錫，備法物，是後不朝侗矣。

translations.literal: The next year he himself called himself Chancellor, received the Nine Bestowals, prepared ritual objects—from then on he did not attend court to Tong.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he made himself chancellor, received the Nine Bestowals, and ceased attending Prince Tong.

sentences.zh: 有道士桓法嗣者，自言解圖讖，世充昵之。

translations.literal: There was a Daoist Huan Fasi who claimed to understand charts and prophecies; Shichong was intimate with him.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist Huan Fasi claimed to read prophecies; Shichong favored him.

sentences.zh: 法嗣乃上《孔子閉房記》，畫作丈夫持一干以驅羊。

translations.literal: Fasi then presented the Record of Confucius Closing the Chamber, painting a man holding a pole driving sheep.
translations.idiomatic: Fasi presented the Record of Confucius Closing the Chamber, showing a man with a pole driving sheep.

sentences.zh: 法嗣云：「楊，隋姓也。

translations.literal: Fasi said: "Yang is the Sui surname.
translations.idiomatic: Fasi said, "Yang is the Sui surname.

sentences.zh: 幹一者，王字也。

translations.literal: Gan one is the character wang.
translations.idiomatic: Gan-yi is the character for wang—king.

sentences.zh: 王居楊後，明相國代隋為帝也。」

translations.literal: Wang dwells after Yang—clearly the chancellor replaces Sui as emperor."
translations.idiomatic: Wang after Yang means the chancellor replaces Sui as emperor."

sentences.zh: 又取《莊子人間世》、《德充符》二篇上之，法嗣釋曰：「上篇言世，下篇言充，此則相國名矣。

translations.literal: Again he took the Zhuangzi chapters "The Human World" and "The Seal of Virtue Complete" and presented them; Fasi explained: "The upper chapter speaks of shi, the lower of chong—this is the chancellor's name.
translations.idiomatic: He cited Zhuangzi's "Human World" and "Seal of Virtue" and explained, "The upper chapter speaks of shi, the lower of chong—this is the chancellor's name.

sentences.zh: 當德被人間，而應符命為天子也。」

translations.literal: He should have virtue filling the human world and respond to the mandate as Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: His virtue would fill the world and he would answer heaven's mandate."

sentences.zh: 世充大悅曰：「此天命也。」

translations.literal: Shichong was greatly pleased and said: "This is Heaven's command."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong was delighted. "This is Heaven's command."

sentences.zh: 再拜受之。

translations.literal: He bowed twice and received it.
translations.idiomatic: He bowed twice and accepted it.

sentences.zh: 即以法嗣為諫議大夫。

translations.literal: He thereupon made Fasi Remonstrance and Counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He made Fasi remonstrance and counsel.

sentences.zh: 世充又羅取雜鳥，書帛系其頸，自言符命而散之於空。

translations.literal: Shichong again gathered miscellaneous birds, wrote on silk and tied it to their necks, claiming mandate of fate and scattering them in the air.
translations.idiomatic: He tied prophecy silk to birds' necks and released them.

sentences.zh: 或有彈射得鳥而來獻者，亦拜官爵。

translations.literal: If some shot down a bird and came to present it, they too were enfeoffed with office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: Those who shot down a bird and brought it were also rewarded with office.

sentences.zh: 既而廢侗，陰殺之，僭即皇帝位，建元曰開明，國號鄭。

translations.literal: Afterward he deposed Tong, secretly killed him, usurped the imperial position, era name Kaiming, state name Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He deposed Tong, killed him secretly, seized the throne with era Kaiming and state name Zheng.

sentences.zh: 大唐太宗帥師圍之。

translations.literal: Great Tang's Prince of Qin led troops to besiege him.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's Prince of Qin besieged him.

sentences.zh: 世充頻出兵，戰輒不利，諸城相繼降款。

translations.literal: Shichong repeatedly sent troops out; each battle was unfavorable and the cities in succession surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sallied again and again and lost; cities surrendered one after another.

sentences.zh: 世充窘迫，遣使請救于竇建德，建德率兵援之。

translations.literal: Shichong in distress sent envoys requesting rescue from Dou Jiande; Jiande led troops to aid him.
translations.idiomatic: Desperate, he begged Dou Jiande for aid; Jiande marched to help.

sentences.zh: 至武牢，太宗破之，禽建德以詣城下。

translations.literal: Reaching Wulao, the Prince of Qin defeated him and seized Jiande to show below the city.
translations.idiomatic: At Wulao the Prince of Qin defeated Jiande and brought him before the walls.

sentences.zh: 世充將潰圍而出，諸將莫有應之者，於是出降。

translations.literal: Shichong wished to break the encirclement and go out; of the generals none responded—thereupon he came out and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong meant to break out; no general would follow—he surrendered.

sentences.zh: 至長安，為仇家所殺。

translations.literal: Reaching Chang'an, he was killed by an enemy family.
translations.idiomatic: At Chang'an an enemy clan killed him.

sentences.zh: 段達，武威姑臧人。

translations.literal: Duan Da was a man of Guzang in Wuwei.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da was from Guzang in Wuwei.

sentences.zh: 父岩，周朔州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yan was Zhou's inspector of Shuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yan was inspector of Shuozhou under Zhou.

sentences.zh: 達在周，年始三歲，襲爵襄坦縣公。

translations.literal: Da in Zhou, at the beginning only three years old, inherited the title Duke of Xiangtan County.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhou he inherited the title Duke of Xiangtan at age three.

sentences.zh: 及長，身長八尺，美須髯，便弓馬。

translations.literal: When grown his body was eight feet, with beautiful beard and whiskers, skilled at bow and horse.
translations.idiomatic: Grown tall with a fine beard, he was expert with bow and horse.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝為丞相，以為大都督，領親信兵，常置左右。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui as chancellor made him Grand Commander, commanding trusted troops, constantly placed at left and right.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen of Sui was chancellor he made Da grand commander of his personal guard.

sentences.zh: 及踐祚，為左直齋，遷車騎將軍，督晉王府軍事。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne he was Left Direct Guard, transferred to Cavalry General, supervising Jin Prince's military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At enthronement he was left direct guard, then cavalry general supervising the Jin prince's forces.

sentences.zh: 以擊高智慧功，授上儀同。

translations.literal: For striking Gao Zhihui he was granted Upper Palace Companion.
translations.idiomatic: For defeating Gao Zhihui he received upper palace companion rank.

sentences.zh: 又破汪文進等，加開府。

translations.literal: Again defeating Wang Wenjin and others, he was added Opening the Government.
translations.idiomatic: Defeating Wang Wenjin and others won him an independent staff.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，為太子左衛副率。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou he was the crown prince's left guard deputy commander.
translations.idiomatic: At Renshou he was the crown prince's left guard deputy.

sentences.zh: 大業初，以籓邸之舊，拜左翊衛將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye, through old ties to the princely residence, he was appointed Left Wing Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: At Daye, through old ties to the prince, he became left wing guard general.

sentences.zh: 從征吐谷渾，進位金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Following the campaign against Tuyuhun he was promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Golden Purple Seal.
translations.idiomatic: On the Tuyuhun campaign he rose to grand master for splendid happiness with the golden purple seal.

sentences.zh: 帝征遼東，平原郝孝德、清河張金稱等並起為盜，帝令達擊之，數為金稱等所挫，諸賊輕之，號為段姥。

translations.literal: The emperor campaigned in Liaodong; Pingyuan's Hao Xiaode, Qinghe's Zhang Jincheng, and others all rose as bandits—the emperor ordered Da to strike them and several times was thwarted by Jincheng and the others; the bandits held him light and called him Old Mother Duan.
translations.idiomatic: On the Liaodong campaign bandits rose; Da was sent against them, was repeatedly beaten by Zhang Jincheng, and the bandits mocked him as Old Mother Duan.

sentences.zh: 後用鄃令楊善會謀，更與賊戰，方致克捷。

translations.literal: Later using Shuxian magistrate Yang Shanhui's plan, he again fought the bandits and at last achieved victory.
translations.idiomatic: Using Yang Shanhui's plan he finally won.

sentences.zh: 還京師，以公事坐免。

translations.literal: Returning to the capital he was dismissed for public affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Back in the capital he was dismissed for an official offense.

sentences.zh: 明年，帝征遼東，使達留守涿郡。

translations.literal: The next year the emperor campaigned in Liaodong and made Da remain to guard Zhuo Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was left to guard Zhuo Commandery during the Liaodong campaign.

sentences.zh: 俄復拜左翊衛將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was again appointed Left Wing Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again made left wing guard general.

sentences.zh: 高陽魏刀兒聚眾，自號曆山飛，寇掠燕、趙。

translations.literal: Gaoyang's Wei Dao'er gathered masses, called himself Flying over the Mountains, and raided Yan and Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Dao'er of Gaoyang gathered a host, styled himself Flying over the Mountains, and raided Yan and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 達率涿郡通守郭絢擊敗之。

translations.literal: Da led Zhuo Commandery transit governor Guo Xuan to defeat him.
translations.idiomatic: Da with Guo Xuan defeated him.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊既多，達不能因機決勝，唯持重自守，時人皆謂之為怯懦。

translations.literal: At that time bandits were already many; Da could not seize the moment for decisive victory but only held heavy and guarded himself—men of the time all called him cowardly.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were everywhere; Da would not risk battle and only held his ground—men called him cowardly.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝幸江都宮，詔達與太府卿元文都等留守東都。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the emperor visited the Jiangdu Palace and ordered Da with Grand Treasury Director Yuan Wendu and others to remain guarding the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year twelve the emperor went to Jiangdu and left Da with Yuan Wendu to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 李密縱兵侵掠城下，達與監門郎將龐玉、武牙郎將霍世舉禦之，以功遷左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Li Mi let troops raid and plunder below the walls; Da with Gate Guard General Pang Yu and Martial Guard General Huo Shiju defended them; for merit he was transferred to Left Valiant Cavalry Guard Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi raided the walls; Da with Pang Yu and Huo Shiju held the city and was made left valiant cavalry grand general.

sentences.zh: 王世充之敗也，密進據北芒，來薄上春門，達與判戶部尚書韋津拒之。

translations.literal: When Wang Shichong was defeated, Mi advanced and held Beimang, coming to press Shangchun Gate; Da with Acting Minister of Revenue Wei Jin resisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong fell, Li Mi held Beimang and pressed Shangchun Gate; Da with Wei Jin resisted.

sentences.zh: 達見賊，不陣而走，軍大潰，津沒於密。

translations.literal: Da saw the bandits and fled without forming battle lines; the army greatly routed and Jin perished in Mi's hands.
translations.idiomatic: Da saw the enemy and fled without forming ranks; the army collapsed and Wei Jin died.

sentences.zh: 及帝崩于江都，達與文都等推越王侗為主，署開府儀同三司，兼納言，陳國公。

translations.literal: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da with Wendu and others pushed Prince Yue Tong as sovereign, appointed Opening the Government with Protocol Equal to Three Offices, concurrently Chief Speaker, Duke of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor died at Jiangdu, Da helped set up Prince Yue Tong as grand master with protocol equal to three offices and chief speaker, Duke of Chen.

sentences.zh: 元文都等之謀誅王世充，達預焉。

translations.literal: Yuan Wendu and the others' plot to execute Wang Shichong—Da took part.
translations.idiomatic: Da took part in Wendu's plot to kill Shichong.

sentences.zh: 既而陰告世充，達為之內應。

translations.literal: Afterward he secretly informed Shichong; Da was his inside responder.
translations.idiomatic: Then he secretly informed Shichong and became his inside man.

sentences.zh: 及事發，迫越王送文都於世充，世充甚德于達。

translations.literal: When the affair broke out he forced Prince Yue to send Wendu to Shichong; Shichong was greatly grateful to Da.
translations.idiomatic: When it broke out he forced the prince to hand Wendu to Shichong, who was deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 既破李密，諷越王禪讓。

translations.literal: After defeating Li Mi he hinted to Prince Yue to abdicate.
translations.idiomatic: After defeating Li Mi he urged the prince to abdicate.

sentences.zh: 世充僭號，以達為司徒。

translations.literal: When Shichong usurped the throne he made Da Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong usurped the throne he made Da minister of education.

sentences.zh: 及東都平，坐斬，妻子籍沒。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was pacified he was executed by beheading; wife and children were registered and confiscated.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital fell he was beheaded and his family confiscated.

sentences.zh: 論曰：宇文述便辟足恭，柔顏取悅。

translations.literal: The commentary says: Yu Wenshu was nimble and obsequious, with feet respectful, soft countenance to win pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Yu Wenshu was obsequious and fawning, ever softening his face to please.

sentences.zh: 君所謂可，亦曰可焉，君所謂不，亦曰不焉。

translations.literal: What the lord called acceptable, he also said was acceptable; what the lord called not, he also said was not.
translations.idiomatic: Whatever the ruler approved he approved; whatever the ruler rejected he rejected.

sentences.zh: 無所是非，不能輕重，默默苟容，偷安高位，甘素餐之責，受彼己之譏。

translations.literal: He had no right or wrong, could not weigh light and heavy, silently endured in tolerance, stole peace in a high post, willingly bore the blame of eating plain rice, and received others' ridicule of himself.
translations.idiomatic: He stood for nothing, weighed nothing, silently clung to office, stole ease in high rank, accepted the shame of an empty salary, and earned the scorn of others.

sentences.zh: 此固君子所不為，亦丘明之深恥。

translations.literal: This is what a gentleman solidly will not do—it is also Qiu Ming's deep shame.
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct a gentleman will not abide; it is what Qiu Ming held in deepest shame.

sentences.zh: 化及以此下才，負恩累葉。

translations.literal: Huaji with this low talent bore ingratitude through accumulated generations.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji, a man of low talent, betrayed favors heaped on his house for generations.

sentences.zh: 時逢崩拆，不能竭命，乃因利乘便，先圖幹紀，率群不逞，職為亂階，擾本塞源，裂冠毀冕。

translations.literal: The time met collapse and splitting; he could not exhaust his life, but took advantage of profit and seized convenience, first scheming to violate discipline, leading the crowd of the unrestrained, his office the steps of chaos, disturbing the root and blocking the source, tearing cap and destroying regalia.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty crumbled he would not give his life; he seized opportunity, plotted first against order, led the lawless as the vanguard of rebellion, upended root and source, and rent crown and regalia.

sentences.zh: 釁深指鹿，事切食蹯，天地所不容，人神所同憤矣，世充頭筲小器，遭逢時幸，與蒙獎擢，禮越舊臣。

translations.literal: The provocation was deep as calling a deer a horse; the affair was urgent as eating a man's flesh—Heaven and Earth could not tolerate it, men and spirits alike were furious. Shichong was a small vessel of a rice-measure cap, who met the age's fortune, together received rewards and promotions, his ritual surpassing old ministers.
translations.idiomatic: His crime was as deep as calling a deer a horse, as vile as devouring human flesh—intolerable to Heaven and Earth, detested by men and spirits alike. Shichong was a petty man of small measure who, meeting a lucky hour, was raised and honored above veteran ministers.

sentences.zh: 而躬為戎首，親行鳩毒。

translations.literal: Yet he personally was the army's head and himself carried out poison-killing.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he himself led the armies and with his own hands wrought murder by poison.

sentences.zh: 竟而蛇豕丑類，繼踵誅夷，梟獍凶魁，相尋菹戮。

translations.literal: In the end the snake-and-boar ugly sort, one after another were executed and exterminated; the owl-and-bear vicious chiefs, in succession were minced and slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: In the end such snake-and-swine villains were cut down one after another, and such owl-and-bear chiefs butchered in turn.

sentences.zh: 垂炯戒于來葉，快忠義于當年，為人臣者，可無殷鑒哉！

translations.literal: They hang bright warnings for coming generations and give satisfaction to loyalty and righteousness in that year—for one who is a minister, can there be no stern mirror!
translations.idiomatic: They leave a bright warning to later ages and gave joy to the loyal in their own day—let any who serve as ministers take this stern mirror to heart!
